title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
副使曹〔子登〕于是合提學副
使李〔汝〕副使嚴〔大紀〕先後所
簡士二千六百有奇鎖院三
試之遵
制額得八十人并錄其文之優
者以
===
獻〔九皐〕猥以執事當序諸首粤
惟河南古豫州域當天地之
中爲陰陽之所和是以士人
生于其閒得中和之氣爲多
在昔名世代作彪炳前聞不
可尚已迨我
國朝
聖祖開基略定中原誕敷
punctuated:
副使曹〔子登〕。于是，合提學副使李〔汝〕、副使嚴〔大紀〕先後所簡士二千六百有奇，鎖院三試之，遵制額得八十人，并錄其文之優者以獻。

〔九皐〕猥以執事，當序諸首。粤惟河南，古豫州域，當天地之中，爲陰陽之所和，是以士人生于其閒，得中和之氣爲多。在昔名世代作，彪炳前聞，不可尚已。迨我國朝聖祖開基，略定中原，誕敷
translation_en:
… Surveillance Vice Commissioner Cao [Zideng]. Thereupon, they gathered the more than two thousand six hundred scholars successively selected by Education-Intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li [Ru] and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Yan [Daji], locked the examination compound, and tested them in three sessions. In accordance with the statutory quota set by imperial decree, they obtained eighty men, and also recorded the superior compositions among their essays to present to the throne.

Unworthily serving in this official capacity, I, [Jiugao], ought to write a preface at the head of this record. Now, Henan is the territory of ancient Yuzhou. Situated at the center of Heaven and Earth, it is the place where Yin and Yang are in harmony. Therefore, the scholars born within this region are richly endowed with the vital energy of centrality and harmony. In antiquity, renowned figures arose generation after generation, shining brightly in the records of the past, such that nothing could surpass them. When it came to our dynasty, the Sacred Ancestor laid the foundations of the empire, pacified the Central Plains, and widely spread …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
文敎暨
列聖紹統累洽重熈建中協和之
化徧于寰區惟此邦之彥埒
于
上國而甲諸省囿地靈致然亦
以
主德茂而沾被渥也茲葢伏遇
===
皇上誕膺
昊眷光撫
洪圖邇者渙頒
宸翰凜數百言首以士習澆漓爲
念又
嘉與臣民更始惓惓于無黨無
偏之訓期底于平平蕩蕩之
punctuated: 文敎，暨列聖紹統，累洽重熈，建中協和之化，徧于寰區。惟此邦之彥，埒于上國，而甲諸省。囿地靈致然，亦以主德茂而沾被渥也。茲葢伏遇皇上誕膺昊眷，光撫洪圖。邇者渙頒宸翰，凜數百言，首以士習澆漓爲念。又嘉與臣民更始，惓惓于「無黨無偏」之訓，期底于「平平蕩蕩」之
translation_en: …literary and moral teaching; and as the successive Sacred Emperors continued the dynastic line through era after era of abundant peace and splendor, the transforming influence of establishing the Mean and harmonizing all things spread throughout the entire realm. Thus the worthy scholars of this region have rivaled those of the capital and stood first among all the provinces. While this is brought about by the auspicious spirit of the land that nurtures them, it is also because the sovereign's virtue is flourishing and the grace they have received is profound. Now, we humbly encounter His Majesty the Emperor, who has grandly received the favor of High Heaven and gloriously governs the great enterprise. Recently, he promulgated an imperial rescript of several hundred awe-inspiring words, making the decadent and superficial customs of the literati his foremost concern. Furthermore, graciously granting a fresh start to his officials and people, he earnestly emphasized the instruction to be "without faction and without bias," hoping to attain the…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
歸所以
建天下中和之極者如日中天
嗚呼麻哉一時僻壤章縫咸
烝烝然會于
皇極漸爲泰龢剗密邇
畿輔嚮德最先如中州之士人
者不將有和其聲以鳴
===
國家之盛者與〔九皐〕幸從校文
後獲覩多士之文類能根極
圖書之藴奥指陳訓命之精
微淵源伊洛之正脉其辭遜
而不阿峻而不亢辯而不訟
核而不誣言人人殊乃其中
和之氣勃不容遏卒澤于道
punctuated: 歸，所以建天下中和之極者，如日中天。嗚呼麻哉！一時僻壤章縫，咸烝烝然會于皇極，漸爲泰龢；剗密邇畿輔、嚮德最先如中州之士人者，不將有和其聲以鳴國家之盛者與？〔九皐〕幸從校文後，獲覩多士之文，類能根極圖書之藴奥，指陳訓命之精微，淵源伊洛之正脉。其辭遜而不阿，峻而不亢，辯而不訟，核而不誣。言人人殊，乃其中和之氣勃不容遏，卒澤于道，
translation_en:
… culmination. Thus, the way in which He establishes the Supreme Standard of equilibrium and harmony for all under Heaven is like the sun at mid-sky. Oh, how auspicious [reading 休 for 麻]! At this time, even the Confucian scholars in remote regions all advance flourishingly to converge upon the August Ultimate, gradually attaining great harmony; how much more so [reading 矧 for 剗] the literati of the Central Plain (Henan), who are in close proximity to the Metropolitan Area and are the very first to turn toward virtue—will they not harmonize their voices to sing of the flourishing of the State?

I, [Jiu]gao, having had the good fortune to participate in the grading of the examination papers, was able to behold the essays of the many scholars. Generally, they are able to probe to the utmost the profound mysteries of the Yellow River Chart and the Luo River Writing, point out and set forth the subtle essentials of the ancient instructions and charges, and trace the orthodox lineage of the Yi-Luo school of learning. Their words are modest without being obsequious, lofty without being arrogant, eloquent without being contentious, and incisive without being unfounded. Though the words differ from person to person, their spirit of equilibrium and harmony bursts forth irrepressibly, ultimately steeped in the Way…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
則較然一也因相與次第錄
之爲之喜而不寐曰茲多士
也異日者服于有位是將能
協恭和衷庶幾哉可少裨
聖天子中和之化矣乎已而懼然
懼曰茲多士也得無有靜言
庸違陷于頗僻果于倖戾者
或奸其間乎審如是
===
國家何賴焉主司又曷以逭其
罪也載惟多士篤生中和之
隩區沐浴中和之
新化所遭固已厚幸矧中和之氣
業已發爲文辭矣固知必爾
爲不也以多士豫產也故不
punctuated: 則較然一也。因相與次第錄之，爲之喜而不寐，曰：「茲多士也，異日者服于有位，是將能協恭和衷，庶幾哉可少裨聖天子中和之化矣乎！」已而懼然懼曰：「茲多士也，得無有靜言庸違，陷于頗僻，果于倖戾者，或奸其間乎？審如是，國家何賴焉？主司又曷以逭其罪也？」載惟多士篤生中和之隩區，沐浴中和之新化，所遭固已厚幸，矧中和之氣業已發爲文辭矣，固知必爾爲不也。以多士豫產也，故不
translation_en: …they are clearly uniform. Thus, together we recorded them in order of rank. Overjoyed by this to the point of sleeplessness, I said: "When these many scholars one day serve in official positions, they will be able to unite in reverence and harmonize their hearts; perhaps they may offer some small aid to the Sacred Son of Heaven's transformative influence of centrality and harmony!" Yet before long, I was seized with apprehension and said in fear: "Among these many scholars, could there not be some who speak smoothly when quiet yet act perversely in practice, who fall into partiality and deviance, or who are resolute in reckless obstinacy [?], illicitly mingling in their midst? If this were truly the case, how could the state rely upon them? And how could the chief examiners escape their guilt?" Yet considering again that these many scholars were born into this heartland of centrality and harmony and have been bathed in the new transformative influence of centrality and harmony, the times they have encountered are already a great fortune; how much more so since the vital energy of centrality and harmony has already manifested itself in their literary compositions! Thus I firmly know that they will certainly not act in such a perverse manner [?]. Because these many scholars are natives of Henan (Yu), I do not…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
厭以中和之説申告云是舉
也巡撫河南右副都御史朱
綱
總理河道兼提督軍務兵
部左侍郎兼右僉都御史萬
恭
提督撫治鄖陽右副都御
史湯〔賓〕宣昭義問丕翼文謨
監察御史清軍余〔乾貞〕印馬
梁〔許〕巡鹽張〔道〕解學禮王〔琢〕
===
王〔肅〕度維風章軌貞敎布政
使司右叅政楊〔俊民〕溫純左
叅議郜〔大經〕朱紹舜按察司
副使楊〔吉〕毛汝賢僉事郭〔孝〕
王〔謠〕徐學詩計〔坤亨〕聶廷璧
都司署都指揮僉事趙〔夢祐〕
punctuated: 厭以中和之説申告云。是舉也，巡撫河南右副都御史朱綱、總理河道兼提督軍務兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史萬恭、提督撫治鄖陽右副都御史湯〔賓〕，宣昭義問，丕翼文謨；監察御史清軍余〔乾貞〕、印馬梁〔許〕、巡鹽張〔道〕，解學禮、王〔琢〕、王〔肅〕度，維風章軌貞敎；布政使司右叅政楊〔俊民〕、溫純，左叅議郜〔大經〕、朱紹舜；按察司副使楊〔吉〕、毛汝賢，僉事郭〔孝〕、王〔謠〕、徐學詩、計〔坤亨〕、聶廷璧；都司署都指揮僉事趙〔夢祐〕、
translation_en:
…tire of reiterating this doctrine of equilibrium and harmony to you.

In this undertaking, Grand Coordinator of Henan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhu Gang 朱綱; Director-General of the Grand Canal and Concurrent Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Left Vice Minister of War, and Concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wan Gong 萬恭; and Military Superintendent and Grand Coordinator of Yunyang and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Tang Bin 湯賓 proclaimed righteous renown and greatly assisted the cultural counsels. Investigating Censors: Troop-Purifying Censor Yu Qianzheng 余乾貞, Horse-Branding Censor Liang Xu 梁許, and Salt-Control Censor Zhang Dao 張道, together with Xie Xueli 解學禮, Wang Zhuo 王琢, and Wang Sudu 王肅度 [?], upheld moral customs, manifested standards, and rectified instruction. From the Provincial Administration Commission, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Yang Junmin 楊俊民 and Wen Chun 溫純, and Left Assistant Administration Commissioners Gao Dajing 郜大經 and Zhu Shaoshun 朱紹舜; from the Provincial Surveillance Commission, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yang Ji 楊吉 and Mao Ruxian 毛汝賢, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Guo Xiao 郭孝, Wang Yao 王謠, Xu Xueshi 徐學詩, Ji Kunheng 計坤亨, and Nie Tingbi 聶廷璧; and from the Regional Military Commission, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Zhao Mengyou 趙夢祐…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
葉〔鎡〕綜理內外防範惟勤右
布政使方〔良曙〕僉事徐〔次翼〕以入
署都指揮僉事胡〔忠〕以入
賀行右參政董〔文寀〕副使章〔時〕
鸞以督賦治河出其以奉
使至者通政使司右通政胡〔執〕
禮光祿寺少卿袁〔三接〕戶部
===
主事劉〔鳳朝〕中書舍人劉〔天〕
衢行人司行人吳〔之美〕李〔丁〕
泰寧侯陳〔良弼〕新寧伯譚〔國〕
佐皆樂觀中土人文之盛者
法得並書
湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭
黎〔九皐〕謹序
punctuated:
葉〔鎡〕，綜理內外，防範惟勤；右布政使方〔良曙〕、僉事徐〔次翼〕以入，署都指揮僉事胡〔忠〕以入賀行；右參政董〔文寀〕、副使章〔時〕鸞以督賦治河出；其以奉使至者，通政使司右通政胡〔執〕禮、光祿寺少卿袁〔三接〕、戶部主事劉〔鳳朝〕、中書舍人劉〔天〕衢、行人司行人吳〔之美〕、李〔丁〕，泰寧侯陳〔良弼〕、新寧伯譚〔國〕佐，皆樂觀中土人文之盛者，法得並書。
湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭黎〔九皐〕謹序。
translation_en:
… and Ye Zi 葉鎡 comprehensively managed internal and external affairs and were diligent in their precautions. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Fang Liangshu 方良曙, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Ciyi 徐次翼, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Hu Zhong 胡忠 had departed to present congratulations at the court [note: the transcription duplicates "以入" across two columns]; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Dong Wencai 董文寀 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Shiluan 章時鸞 were away on assignment supervising tax collection and managing the Yellow River; and as for those who arrived on imperial missions—Right Transmission Commissioner of the Office of Transmission Hu Zhili 胡執禮, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yuan Sanjie 袁三接, Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue Liu Fengchao 劉鳳朝, Drafter Liu Tianqu 劉天衢, Messengers of the Messenger Office Wu Zhimei 吳之美 and Li Ding 李丁, Marquis of Taining Chen Liangbi 陳良弼, and Earl of Xinning Tan Guozuo 譚國佐—all took pleasure in witnessing the flourishing of literary culture in the Central Plains, and by rule they should all be recorded together.

Respectfully prefaced by Li Jiugao 黎九皐, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yizhang County in Chenzhou Subprefecture, Huguang.

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年河南鄉試
監臨官
巡按河南監察御史褚　鈇〔民威山西榆次縣人　乙丑進士〕
提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使吴道直〔敬甫直隸定州人　癸丑進士〕
河南等處承宣布政使司左參政馮敏功〔元卿浙江平湖縣人　壬戌進士〕
監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使鮑承蔭〔子傳山西長治縣人　丙辰進士〕
河南等處提刑按察司副使曹子登〔以漸直隸興州後屯衛　籍長洲縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭黎允皐〔聞遠廣西臨桂縣人　甲子貢士〕
應天府六合縣儒學教諭吴　邦〔子經浙江錢塘縣人　甲子貢士〕
同考試官
直隸永平府儒學教授趙崇典〔懋章廣東東莞縣人　壬子貢士〕
直隸廣平府儒學教授高鵬霄〔鯤化山東丘縣人　丙午貢士〕
山西平陽府儒學教授紀　會〔應期陝西洋縣人　壬子貢士〕
陝西西安府涇陽縣儒學教諭陳一濂〔子濬四川巴州人　癸卯貢士〕
廣西柳州府洛容縣儒學教諭何　鐈〔尚釆廣西懷集縣人　戊午貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆元年河南鄉試

監臨官
巡按河南監察御史褚鈇〔民威，山西榆次縣人，乙丑進士。〕

提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使吴道直〔敬甫，直隸定州人，癸丑進士。〕
河南等處承宣布政使司左參政馮敏功〔元卿，浙江平湖縣人，壬戌進士。〕

監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使鮑承蔭〔子傳，山西長治縣人，丙辰進士。〕
河南等處提刑按察司副使曹子登〔以漸，直隸興州後屯衛籍，長洲縣人，壬戌進士。〕

考試官
湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭黎允皐〔聞遠，廣西臨桂縣人，甲子貢士。〕
應天府六合縣儒學教諭吴邦〔子經，浙江錢塘縣人，甲子貢士。〕

同考試官
直隸永平府儒學教授趙崇典〔懋章，廣東東莞縣人，壬子貢士。〕
直隸廣平府儒學教授高鵬霄〔鯤化，山東丘縣人，丙午貢士。〕
山西平陽府儒學教授紀會〔應期，陝西洋縣人，壬子貢士。〕
陝西西安府涇陽縣儒學教諭陳一濂〔子濬，四川巴州人，癸卯貢士。〕
廣西柳州府洛容縣儒學教諭何鐈〔尚釆，廣西懷集縣人，戊午貢士。〕
translation_en:
Henan Provincial Examination of the First Year of the Wanli Era (1573)

Supervising Official (監臨官)
Chu Fu 褚鈇, Regional Inspector of Henan and Investigating Censor. 〔Courtesy name Minwei 民威; a native of Yuci County, Shanxi; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year (1565).〕

Proctors (提調官)
Wu Daozhi 吴道直, Left Administration Commissioner of the Henan Provincial Administration Commission. 〔Courtesy name Jingfu 敬甫; a native of Dingzhou, Zhili; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year (1553).〕
Feng Mingong 馮敏功, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Henan Provincial Administration Commission. 〔Courtesy name Yuanqing 元卿; a native of Pinghu County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562).〕

Monitoring Officials (監試官)
Bao Chengyin 鮑承蔭, Surveillance Commissioner of the Henan Provincial Surveillance Commission. 〔Courtesy name Zichuan 子傳; a native of Changzhi County, Shanxi; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year (1556).〕
Cao Zideng 曹子登, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Henan Provincial Surveillance Commission. 〔Courtesy name Yijian 以漸; registered in the Xingzhou Rear Tun Guard in Zhili, originally a native of Changzhou County; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562).〕

Examiners (考試官)
Li Yungao 黎允皐, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yizhang County, Chenzhou, Huguang. 〔Courtesy name Wenyuan 聞遠; a native of Lingui County, Guangxi; tribute scholar (gongshi, i.e., provincial graduate) of the jiazi year (1564).〕
Wu Bang 吴邦, Instructor in the Confucian School of Liuhe County, Yingtian Prefecture. 〔Courtesy name Zijing 子經; a native of Qiantang County, Zhejiang; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year (1564).〕

Associate Examiners (同考試官)
Zhao Chongdian 趙崇典, Professor in the Confucian School of Yongping Prefecture, Zhili. 〔Courtesy name Maozhang 懋章; a native of Dongguan County, Guangdong; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year (1552).〕
Gao Pengxiao 高鵬霄, Professor in the Confucian School of Guangping Prefecture, Zhili. 〔Courtesy name Kunhua 鯤化; a native of Qiu County, Shandong; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year (1546).〕
Ji Hui 紀會, Professor in the Confucian School of Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. 〔Courtesy name Yingqi 應期; a native of Yang County, Shaanxi; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year (1552).〕
Chen Yilian 陳一濂, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jingyang County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. 〔Courtesy name Zijun 子濬; a native of Bazhou, Sichuan; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the guimao year (1543).〕
He Jiao 何鐈, Instructor in the Confucian School of Luorong County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. 〔Courtesy name Shangcai 尚釆; a native of Huaiji County, Guangxi; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuwu year (1558).〕

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
河南等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷成敏覺〔任卿湖廣石首縣人 監生〕
河南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事桂學斯〔用信江西上饒縣人 監生〕
收掌試卷官

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君賜食必正席先嘗之
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
民事不可緩也詩云晝爾于茅宵爾索綯
亟其乘屋其始播百穀
易
聖人作而萬物覩
利見大人亨聚以正也
===
問焉而以言其受命也如嚮无有遠近幽
深遂知來物
天地之大德曰生
書
九敘惟歌戒之用休董之用威勸之以九
歌
伊洛瀍澗既入于河
監于先王成憲其永無愆惟說式克欽承
旁招俊乂列于庶位
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
君賜食，必正席先嘗之。
齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。
民事不可緩也。《詩》云：「晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯；亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。」

易：
聖人作而萬物覩。
利見大人，亨，聚以正也。
問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。
天地之大德曰生。

書：
九敘惟歌。戒之用休，董之用威，勸之以九歌。
伊、洛、瀍、澗既入于河。
監于先王成憲，其永無愆。惟說式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu):
"When the ruler sent him a gift of cooked food, he would always straighten his mat and be the first to taste it."
"Fasting, purifying oneself, and putting on ceremonial attire, and not making any movement contrary to the rites: this is the way to cultivate the person."
"The business of the people may not be delayed. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: 'In the day go and gather the thatch-grass; in the night twist your ropes; then make haste to get upon the roofs;—for now you must begin again to sow the hundred grains.'"

The Book of Changes (Yi):
"When the Sage arises, the myriad things look toward him."
"'It is advantageous to see the Great Man; there will be success': their gathering together is by means of uprightness."
"When one puts a question to it and it speaks, it receives the command like an echo; whether the matter is far or near, obscure or deep, it thereupon makes known the things to come."
"The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called the giving of life."

The Book of Documents (Shu):
"When the nine services all have their orderly arrangement, this may be sung of. Admonish them with what is admirable, correct them with majesty, and encourage them with the nine songs."
"The Yi, Luo, Chan, and Jian rivers had already been conducted into the Yellow River."
"Taking the established statutes of the former kings as a mirror, you will forever be free from fault. And I, Yue, shall thereby be able reverently to obey your charge, extensively summoning men of eminent ability and placing them in the various official positions." …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
詩
游環脅驅陰靷鋈續
鶴鳴于九臯聲聞于天魚在于渚或潛在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山
之石可以攻玉
昭兹來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
成王不敢康夙夜基命宥密
===
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊〕
公十有三年
冬十月不雨〔僖公二年〕春王正月不雨夏
四月不雨　六月雨〔俱僖公三年〕
秋楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋〔襄公元年〕
元年　春王正月〔俱隱公元年〕楚屈完來
盟于師〔僖公四年〕齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰
田〔定公十年〕
punctuated:
小大之臣，咸懷忠良；其侍御僕從，罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。

詩：
「游環脅驅，陰靷鋈續。」
「鶴鳴于九臯，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潛在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。」
「昭兹來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。」
「成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。」

春秋：
「春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。」〔莊公十有三年〕
「冬，十月，不雨。」〔僖公二年〕「春，王正月，不雨。夏，四月，不雨。」　「六月，雨。」〔俱僖公三年〕
「秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋。」〔襄公元年〕
「元年，」　「春，王正月。」〔俱隱公元年〕「楚屈完來盟于師。」〔僖公四年〕「齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。」〔定公十年〕
translation_en:
"The ministers, great and small, will all cherish loyalty and goodness; the attendants and servants will none of them be other than upright men, who morning and evening will support and assist their sovereign."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"With slip-rings and side-straps, and traces attached to the front-board with gilt rings."
"The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the heavens. The fish lies by the islet, or sinks in the deep pool. Pleasant is that garden, in which are planted sandalwood trees, and beneath them is the paper-mulberry. The stones of other hills may be used to polish jade."
"Brightly he advances upon this path, continuing the footsteps of his ancestors. For ten thousand years, may he receive the blessings of Heaven!"
"cheng Wang did not dare to take his ease; morning and night he laid the foundations of the mandate in profundity and quietude."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In spring, the Marquis of Qi, a man of Song, a man of Chen, a man of Cai, and a man of Zhu met at Beixing." [13th year of Duke Zhuang]
"In winter, in the tenth month, it did not rain." [2nd year of Duke Xi] "In spring, in the King's first month, it did not rain. In summer, in the fourth month, it did not rain." "In the sixth month, it rained." [All from the 3rd year of Duke Xi]
"In autumn, Gongzi Renfu of Chu led an army and invaded Song." [1st year of Duke Xiang]
"First year," "In spring, the King's first month." [Both from the 1st year of Duke Yin] "Qu Wan of Chu came and made a covenant with the army." [4th year of Duke Xi] "Men of Qi came and restored the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin." [10th year of Duke Ding]

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
禮記
趨以采齊行以肆夏周還中規折還中矩
進則揖之退則揚之然後玉鏘鳴也
大人舉禮樂則天地將爲昭焉
以事天地山川社稷先古以爲醴酪齊盛
於是乎取之敬之至也
故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功是以國安
而君寧
第貳場
===
論
仁者以天地萬物爲一體
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元和十年〕
擬輔臣進
帝鑑圖說表〔萬曆元年〕
判語〔五條〕
punctuated:
《禮記》
趨以《采齊》，行以《肆夏》，周還中規，折還中矩，進則揖之，退則揚之，然後玉鏘鳴也。
大人舉禮樂，則天地將爲昭焉。
以事天地、山川、社稷、先古，以爲醴酪齊盛，於是乎取之，敬之至也。
故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功，是以國安而君寧。

第貳場
論：
仁者以天地萬物爲一體。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕。
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元和十年〕。
擬輔臣進《帝鑑圖說》表〔萬曆元年〕。

判語〔五條〕：
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"They hastened to the music of the 'Caiqi' and walked to the music of the 'Sixia.' Their circular turns matched the compass, and their angular turns matched the carpenter's square. Advancing, they bowed slightly forward; retiring, they held their heads high; and thus their jade pendants tinkled in harmony."
"When the great man puts rites and music into practice, Heaven and Earth will thereby be made bright and clear."
"To serve Heaven and Earth, the mountains and rivers, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancient ancestors, and to prepare sweet wine, soured milk, and sacrificial grain in vessels—all these are derived from this; it is the utmost degree of reverence."
"Therefore, ministers and subordinates all strive to exhaust their strength and use their abilities to the fullest in order to establish merit; thus the state is secure and the ruler enjoys peace."

Second Session
Discourse (lun):
"The humane person regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body."

Edict, Mandate, or Memorial [answer one of the following]:
Compose in imitation an edict of the Han dynasty deliberating on relief and loans during the geniality of spring [first year of Emperor Wen (179 BCE)].
Compose in imitation a mandate of the Tang dynasty appointing Pei Du 裴度 as Vice Director of the Secretariat (zhongshu shilang) and Jointly Manager of Affairs (tong pingzhangshi) [tenth year of the Yuanhe era (815)].
Compose in imitation a memorial by the Grand Secretaries presenting the Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tushuo) [first year of the Wanli era (1573)].

Legal Judgments [five items]: …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
封掌印信
轉解官物
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
冒破物料
第叄場
策五道
問聖主待賢臣而弘功業俊士俟明主以
顯其德其相須亦甚殷矣考之唐虞三
===
代君臣交儆都俞吁咈載在典謨訓誥
者邈乎不可尚已嗣是英君賢臣有講
論經理夜分乃寐者有論道延英日昃
不倦者有日御經筵重陽不輟者有進
講無逸直至終篇者果如唐虞三代之
君之〔諮〕諮其臣否乎有選賢良而陳射〔譬〕
傷業者有對玉階而諫日昃方起者有
召講御閣而對以剛健決事者有賜坐
崇政而對以明王愛民者果如唐虞三
punctuated:
封掌印信。
轉解官物。
服舍違式。
優恤軍屬。
冒破物料。

第叄場

策五道

問：聖主待賢臣而弘功業，俊士俟明主以顯其德，其相須亦甚殷矣。考之唐虞三代，君臣交儆，都俞吁咈，載在《典》《謨》《訓》《誥》者，邈乎不可尚已。嗣是英君賢臣，有講論經理、夜分乃寐者，有論道延英、日昃不倦者，有日御經筵、重陽不輟者，有進講《無逸》、直至終篇者，果如唐虞三代之君之〔諮〕諮其臣否乎？有選賢良而陳射〔譬〕傷業者，有對玉階而諫日昃方起者，有召講御閣而對以剛健決事者，有賜坐崇政而對以明王愛民者，果如唐虞三…
translation_en:
Sealing and keeping custody of official seals.
Forwarding and delivering government property.
Clothing and housing in violation of regulations.
Compassionate relief for military dependents.
Fraudulent claims for wasted materials.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: A sage ruler awaits worthy ministers to broaden his achievements, while men of outstanding talent await an enlightened ruler to manifest their virtue; their mutual dependence is indeed most profound! Examining the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, sovereign and minister mutually admonished one another, expressing agreement and disagreement with "Oh!", "Yes!", "Alas!", and "Nay!"; what is recorded in the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements is so lofty and distant that nothing can surpass it. After those times, among heroic rulers and worthy ministers, there was one who discussed the principles of governance and classics until midnight before sleeping; one who discussed the Way in the Yanying Hall without tiring until the sun tilted westward; one who attended the Classics Colloquium daily without stopping even on the Double Ninth festival; and one who had the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) expounded straight through to the end of the chapter—were they truly like the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties in consulting [?] their ministers? There was one who, selected as Worthy and Good, set forth metaphors [?] about harming one's enterprise; one who replied before the jade steps to remonstrate against rising only when the sun was already past noon; one who was summoned to lecture in the Imperial Pavilion and replied with advice on deciding affairs with resolute vigor; and one who was granted a seat in the Chongzheng Hall and replied that an enlightened king loves the people—were they truly like the [ministers of] Tang, Yu, and the Three…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
代之臣之啓其君否乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝聘四儒而
賜坐延訪
成祖文皇帝嘉六臣而
寵賚優厚
列聖相承丕隆繼述
明良交際遠追唐虞三代之盛矣迨我
皇上秉
上聖之資撫
===
中興之運日
御文華時親
講幄繹聖經而講解不倦灑
宸翰而綱誨是期一時
廷臣莫不感激思以自
獻至於繪圖分類啓沃
聖心其與君臣交儆之風實同一轍然忠臣愛
君無已所以涵養
君心贊襄
punctuated: 代之臣之啓其君否乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝聘四儒而賜坐延訪，成祖文皇帝嘉六臣而寵賚優厚。列聖相承，丕隆繼述，明良交際，遠追唐、虞、三代之盛矣。迨我皇上，秉上聖之資，撫中興之運，日御文華，時親講幄，繹聖經而講解不倦，灑宸翰而綱誨是期。一時廷臣莫不感激，思以自獻，至於繪圖分類，啓沃聖心，其與君臣交儆之風，實同一轍。然忠臣愛君無已，所以涵養君心、贊襄
translation_en: … ministers of the [Three] Dynasties enlightened their sovereigns? Reflecting upon how our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), invited the Four Scholars and granted them seats to inquire of them at length, and how our Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu), commended the Six Ministers and bestowed upon them generous favors and rewards—successive sacred emperors have inherited this legacy, greatly exalting the continuation of their predecessors' work, so that the communion between enlightened sovereigns and worthy ministers has reached far back to match the flourishing eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Now, our present Emperor, endowed with supreme sagehood and presiding over an era of dynastic revival, daily attends the Wenhua Hall and frequently approaches the lecturing tent, unraveling the sacred classics and explaining them tirelessly, and wielding the imperial brush in hopes of receiving guiding instruction [?]. At present, there is no court minister who is not moved to gratitude and eager to offer his own counsel, even to the point of painting illustrations and arranging them by category to enlighten and nourish the Sacred Mind—which truly follows the same track as the ancient custom of sovereign and minister mutually admonishing one another. Yet a loyal minister's love for his sovereign is unending; as for the means of nurturing the sovereign's mind and assisting in …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖化者不知於
經筵之外更有所當務者與願詳言之以爲
聖天子保治之助
問
宗藩
帝室之裔自昔敦睦九族推恩莫先焉漢初諸
侯王置吏握兵而末大不掉唐鑒前轍
流播民間至宋聚族京師騷然繁費制
有厚薄而流弊因之其何道而可與我
===
太祖高皇帝開天啓運
成祖文皇帝定鼎奠基乃分建
諸王環輩疆宇制祿之法皆歲給五萬石其
恩施固孔渥矣厥後大司農告艱不數歲而減
至萬石今
熙洽二百餘年瓜瓞綿衍不啻百倍竭〔編〕〔畊〕
之力以爲供則十室九空舉支庶之衆
以望哺則束手枵腹即桑孔握籌必不
能兩利而兼得也說者謂宜限爵似矣
punctuated:
聖化者，不知於經筵之外更有所當務者與？願詳言之，以爲聖天子保治之助。

問：宗藩，帝室之裔，自昔敦睦九族，推恩莫先焉。漢初諸侯王置吏握兵，而末大不掉；唐鑒前轍，流播民間；至宋聚族京師，騷然繁費。制有厚薄，而流弊因之，其何道而可與？我太祖高皇帝開天啓運，成祖文皇帝定鼎奠基，乃分建諸王，環輩疆宇，制祿之法，皆歲給五萬石，其恩施固孔渥矣。厥後大司農告艱，不數歲而減至萬石。今熙洽二百餘年，瓜瓞綿衍，不啻百倍。竭〔編〕〔畊〕之力以爲供，則十室九空；舉支庶之衆以望哺，則束手枵腹。即桑、孔握籌，必不能兩利而兼得也。說者謂宜限爵，似矣；
translation_en:
… Imperial transformative influence—one wonders whether beyond the Classics Colloquia there are still other matters that should be attended to? I hope you will speak of this in detail, as an aid to the Sacred Son of Heaven in preserving good governance.

Question: The imperial clansmen enfeoffed in the feudatories are descendants of the imperial house; since antiquity, in cultivating harmony among the nine grades of kinsmen, nothing has taken precedence over extending grace to them. In the early Han, the kings and marquises appointed officials and commanded troops, so that the branches grew too large for the trunk to sway; the Tang, taking warning from the tracks of its predecessor, left them scattered among the common people; by the Song, the clan was gathered together in the capital, causing disturbance and heavy expense. Whether the system was generous or stingy, abuses followed accordingly—by what way, then, can this be managed properly? When Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), opened Heaven and initiated the dynastic fortune, and the Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu), established the tripods and laid the foundations, they enfeoffed the princes in domains ringing the realm like a belt [? 環輩, likely for 環衛, guarding the borders], and under the regulations for their stipends each was granted fifty thousand piculs (shi) of grain a year—a bestowal of grace that was truly most abundant. Thereafter the Grand Minister of Agriculture reported fiscal difficulties, and within a few years the stipends were reduced to ten thousand piculs. Now, after more than two hundred years of prosperous peace, the royal descendants have multiplied like trailing melon vines to more than a hundredfold. If we exhaust the strength of the registered cultivators [? 〔編〕〔畊〕] to supply them, nine out of ten households are left empty; yet if all the multitude of collateral and secondary kinsmen look for sustenance, they are left with hands bound and stomachs empty. Even if Sang Hongyang 桑弘羊 and Kong Jin 孔僅 held the counting rods, they certainly could not secure both advantages at once. Commentators say that peerage ranks should be limited, which seems plausible; …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
然繫名
玉牒者皆
天潢系胤使無
一命之榮可乎謂宜限祿似矣然子姓鱗列阨
體告哀使無計口之儲可乎謂宜弛其
出城諸禁似矣然越關四出疲於奔命
能保無他虞乎玆一時權宜之計其於
祖宗成法合與否耶抑通變宜時亦有必不得
已者與今欲補偏捄弊使經久可行必
===
何如而後可
宗冑之繁中州爲最爾諸士目擊心惟抱杞
人之憂久矣請詳著於篇以觀經濟之
學
問周禮一書周公致太平之法也其綱領
見於周官其條目載於六典大經旣舉
庶務畢張聖王制治之良規燦然備矣
或者乃指爲成周理財之書其說果何
所據而甚則詆之爲戰國陰謀之書又

===
何如而後可
宗胄之繁中州爲最爾諸士目擊心惟抱杞
人之憂久矣請詳著於篇以觀經濟之
學
問周禮一書周公致太平之法也其綱領
見於周官其條目載於六典大經旣舉
庶務畢張聖王制治之良規燦然備矣
或者乃指爲成周理財之書其說果何
所據而甚則詆之爲戰國陰謀之書又
punctuated:
然繫名玉牒者，皆天潢系胤，使無一命之榮，可乎？謂宜限祿，似矣；然子姓鱗列，阨體告哀，使無計口之儲，可乎？謂宜弛其出城諸禁，似矣；然越關四出，疲於奔命，能保無他虞乎？玆一時權宜之計，其於祖宗成法合與否耶？抑通變宜時，亦有必不得已者與？今欲補偏捄弊，使經久可行，必何如而後可？宗冑之繁，中州爲最。爾諸士目擊心惟，抱杞人之憂久矣，請詳著於篇，以觀經濟之學。
問：《周禮》一書，周公致太平之法也。其綱領見於《周官》，其條目載於六典。大經旣舉，庶務畢張，聖王制治之良規，燦然備矣。或者乃指爲成周理財之書，其說果何所據？而甚則詆之爲戰國陰謀之書，又
translation_en:
… Yet those whose names are registered in the Jade Genealogies are all descendants of the imperial lineage; would it do to leave them without the honor of even the lowest official rank? Some say their stipends ought to be limited, which seems plausible; yet when descendants are arrayed like fish scales and cry out in distress from bodily privation, would it do to leave them without provisions calculated per capita? Some say the various prohibitions against their leaving the walled cities ought to be relaxed, which seems plausible; yet if they cross the passes and go out in all directions, exhausting people in rushing about at their command, can one guarantee there will be no other unforeseen dangers? Do these expedient measures of the moment accord with the established laws of the Imperial Ancestors or not? Or, in adapting to changing circumstances to suit the times, are there also things that simply cannot be avoided? If we now wish to rectify imbalances and remedy abuses so as to make the system viable for the long term, how must we proceed before it will work? The proliferation of imperial clansmen is greatest in the Central Plain (Henan). You gentlemen have witnessed this with your own eyes and pondered it in your hearts, harboring anxiety like the man of Qi for a long time now. Please set forth your views in detail in your essays, so that we may observe your learning in statecraft.

Question: The Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) is the method by which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Its guiding principles appear in the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan), and its detailed articles are recorded in the Six Statutes. Once the great norms are raised up, all administrative affairs are fully extended; the fine regulations by which the sage kings instituted governance are resplendently complete therein. Yet some point to it as a book on fiscal administration in the Zhou dynasty—upon what is this theory actually based? And going even further, some slander it as a book of Warring States intrigues—how, moreover, …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
何其敢於誣聖也好古之士賭其全而
不得乃以考工記補之是果足為周禮
之全書乎今以周官考之則六官之職
固自有在其果缺耶否耶即以六屬計
之則三百六十之官各有攸司又何五
官之復多餘羨耶後世亦有倣而行之
者而卒無裨於治豈古今之不相為謀
抑此書之不足於用耶夫窮經將以致
用諸士子近成周之居學周〔公之道久〕
===
矣請詳著之以觀用世之學
問黃河之患自古有之禹績以來在殷商
時已被其害及從砱礫勢益變遷自漢
而後講求頗詳無能出賈讓三策者宋
人都汴防禦益切自天聖迄於宣和聚
訟盈庭國是靡定我
國家轉漕東南以餉
京邊所藉尤重然自張秋以後勞費滋大中
土之患亦至殷矣迨於近歲河患在徐
punctuated:
何其敢於誣聖也？好古之士，賭其全而不得，乃以《考工記》補之，是果足為《周禮》之全書乎？今以《周官》考之，則六官之職固自有在，其果缺耶？否耶？即以六屬計之，則三百六十之官各有攸司，又何五官之復多餘羨耶？後世亦有倣而行之者，而卒無裨於治，豈古今之不相為謀，抑此書之不足於用耶？夫窮經將以致用，諸士子近成周之居，學周〔公之道久〕矣，請詳著之，以觀用世之學。

問：黃河之患，自古有之。禹績以來，在殷商時已被其害，及從砱礫，勢益變遷。自漢而後，講求頗詳，無能出賈讓三策者。宋人都汴，防禦益切，自天聖迄於宣和，聚訟盈庭，國是靡定。我國家轉漕東南，以餉京、邊，所藉尤重；然自張秋以後，勞費滋大，中土之患亦至殷矣。迨於近歲，河患在徐、
translation_en:
…how dare they so slander the Sage! Scholars fond of antiquity, unable to see the work in its entirety, supplemented it with the Record of Trades (Kaogong ji). Does this truly suffice to make the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) a complete book? If we examine it today in light of the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhouguan), the duties of the Six Offices are already present in their own right—were they truly missing, or not? And if we reckon by the six subordinate hierarchies, the three hundred and sixty offices each have their own responsibilities; why then is there still such a surplus of offices across the remaining five ministries? In later ages there were also those who imitated and put it into practice, yet in the end it brought no benefit to governance. Is it that past and present cannot take counsel from one another, or that this book is inadequate for practical use? Now, mastering the Classics is meant for practical application. You gentlemen live near the seat of the Accomplished Zhou and have studied [the Way of the Duke] of Zhou [for a long time]. Please set forth your views in detail, so that we may observe your learning for practical statecraft.

Question: The disasters of the Yellow River have existed since antiquity. Since the achievements of Yu, people already suffered its harm during the Yin-Shang period, and after the river shifted at Leli [?], its course changed ever more radically. From the Han dynasty onward, the matter was investigated in considerable detail, yet no one was able to surpass the three strategies of Jia Rang. When the Song made Bian their capital, defense against the river became even more urgent; from the Tiansheng (1023–1032) to the Xuanhe (1119–1125) eras, conflicting arguments filled the court and state policy remained unsettled. Our Dynasty transports tribute grain by water from the southeast to provision the capital and the frontiers, relying upon the river all the more heavily. Yet since the breach at Zhangqiu, the labor and expense have grown increasingly vast, and the affliction to the Central Plains has also been extreme. Coming down to recent years, the river's disasters have been located between Xuzhou and…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
邳間中土稍得休息然運道數阻
廟議孔艱乃以部臣親出經理一時大小河
臣矢心宣力殫悉疏防幸底安流漕艘
畢達向者欲開膠河泇河通運之說已
無容議矣然河性不常乍淤乍決何以
俾河道之常安河流迅駛險惡萬狀何
以保運艘之無失又謂海口沙墊欲開
濬以導其流又謂河勢浩猛欲分疏以
殺其勢其說果可行乎抑別有救時之
===
策可以爲經久之規矣乎其他自漢而
下治河之議亦有可採而行之者乎諸
士生於中土目擊河患當必有博詢遠
計以輔吾聞見之所不逮者幸詳言之
毋忽
問將者三軍之司命擇之貴豫任之貴專
昔之論將者言人人殊試舉一二與諸
士子商之武成王曰將有五才而孫吳
之說則又有曰仁智信勇嚴理備果戒
punctuated:
邳間，中土稍得休息。然運道數阻，廟議孔艱，乃以部臣親出經理，一時大小河臣矢心宣力，殫悉疏防，幸底安流，漕艘畢達。向者欲開膠河、泇河通運之說，已無容議矣。然河性不常，乍淤乍決，何以俾河道之常安？河流迅駛，險惡萬狀，何以保運艘之無失？又謂海口沙墊，欲開濬以導其流；又謂河勢浩猛，欲分疏以殺其勢。其說果可行乎？抑別有救時之策，可以爲經久之規矣乎？其他自漢而下治河之議，亦有可採而行之者乎？諸士生於中土，目擊河患，當必有博詢遠計，以輔吾聞見之所不逮者，幸詳言之，毋忽。

問：將者，三軍之司命，擇之貴豫，任之貴專。昔之論將者，言人人殊，試舉一二與諸士子商之。武成王曰「將有五才」，而孫、吳之說則又有曰「仁、智、信、勇、嚴」、「理、備、果、戒、
translation_en:
… between Xuzhou 徐州 and Pizhou 邳州, so the Central Plains have enjoyed a brief respite. Yet the grain-transport waterway has repeatedly been blocked, and court deliberations proved exceedingly difficult. Thereupon a ministerial official was dispatched in person to take charge of management, and for a time the river-control officials, great and small, pledged their hearts and exerted their strength, exhausting every effort in dredging and diking. Fortunately the river was brought to a peaceful flow, and the grain-transport barges all reached their destination. The earlier proposals to excavate the Jiao River 膠河 and the Jia River 泇河 to open alternative transport routes now require no further discussion. Yet the nature of the Yellow River is inconstant, suddenly silting up and suddenly breaching its banks—how can the river course be kept permanently secure? The river's current is swift and fierce, presenting ten thousand forms of peril—how can the transport barges be guaranteed against loss? Some also say that the mouth of the river at the sea is choked with sand and wish to excavate and dredge it to guide the flow; others say that the force of the river is vast and violent and wish to divide and channel it in order to weaken its momentum. Are these proposals truly feasible? Or is there some other measure to save the present situation that can serve as a permanent standard? As for other discussions on river control from the Han dynasty down, are there any among them that can be adopted and put into practice? You gentlemen were born in the Central Plains and have witnessed the disasters of the river with your own eyes; you must certainly possess broad inquiries and far-reaching plans to supplement what our own hearing and sight have failed to reach. Please set them forth in detail, and do not be negligent.

Question: The general is the arbiter of fate for the Three Armies; selecting him requires advance preparation, and employing him requires undivided authority. Those who discussed generals in the past differed from person to person in their words; let us raise one or two points to deliberate with you gentlemen. King Wucheng 武成王 [Jiang Ziya 姜子牙] said that "a general has five talents," whereas in the doctrines of Sun Wu 孫武 and Wu Qi 吳起 there are also the sayings "benevolence, wisdom, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness" and "order, preparedness, decisiveness, vigilance, and …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
約者何若是其不同也又有分之爲賢
將才將者夫將一也而乃有賢將才將
之分果當與否與自漢以下若寄食淮
濵者功成垓下奴隷主家者動勒狼胥
豈其儲之亦豫乎若市租入府而備邊
破狄三科募士而增竈破羌豈其任之
者別有其道乎方今
聖皇愼德四夷咸賔邊壓固巳敉寧矣然思患
豫防尤
===
聖世所當先圖者邇者特廑
宸慮遣大臣行邊親閱又屢
允言官之請
令九卿百司各舉所知但不識其所選者果
以何者爲準與其任之者果有得于古
人之法否與諸士子志在匡時願悉言
之以副
當宁拊髀之思毋曰非其職也諉之
punctuated: 約者，何若是其不同也？又有分之爲賢將、才將者。夫將一也，而乃有賢將、才將之分，果當與否與？自漢以下，若寄食淮濵者，功成垓下；奴隷主家者，動勒狼胥，豈其儲之亦豫乎？若市租入府而備邊破狄，三科募士而增竈破羌，豈其任之者別有其道乎？方今聖皇愼德，四夷咸賔，邊壓固巳敉寧矣。然思患豫防，尤聖世所當先圖者。邇者特廑宸慮，遣大臣行邊親閱，又屢允言官之請，令九卿百司各舉所知。但不識其所選者果以何者爲準與？其任之者果有得于古人之法否與？諸士子志在匡時，願悉言之，以副當宁拊髀之思，毋曰非其職也，諉之。
translation_en:
… and restraint." Why do these accounts differ so greatly? Furthermore, there are those who divide them into "worthy generals" (xianjiang) and "talented generals" (caijiang). Now, the office of general is one; is it truly appropriate or not to divide them into worthy generals and talented generals? From the Han dynasty onward, there were men like he who begged for food by the banks of the Huai River [Han Xin 韓信] yet achieved victory at Gaixia, and he who was a slave in a princess's household [Huo Qubing 霍去病] yet inscribed his exploits on Mount Langju [written 狼胥, likely for 狼居胥; 動 likely a misprint for 勳]; could it be that they too had been cultivated in advance? And as for he who took the market tax revenues into his commandery headquarters [Li Mu 李牧] to guard the frontier and rout the northern tribes, or he who recruited soldiers under three categories and increased the number of camp stoves to defeat the Qiang [Yu Xu 虞詡], could it be that those who employed them had some special way of doing so?

At present, Our Sacred Emperor is circumspect in his virtue, the barbarians of the四 quarters all submit as guests, and the frontier territories [邊壓, likely a misprint for 邊疆 or 邊鄙] are indeed already pacified and tranquil. Yet taking thought of potential calamities and guarding against them in advance is all the more what a sacred age ought to plan for first. Recently, this has particularly engaged the imperial concern: high ministers have been dispatched to tour the frontiers and inspect them in person, and the Emperor has repeatedly approved the requests of speaking officials, ordering the Nine Chief Ministers and the various offices each to recommend those whom they know. However, one wonders: by what standard should those whom they select truly be measured? And does the manner in which they are employed truly capture the methods of the ancients or not? You gentlemen aspire to rectify the times; I hope you will speak of this in full, so as to answer the sovereign's longing [as when Emperor Wen of Han slapped his thigh thinking of fine generals], and do not shirk the question by saying it does not pertain to your office.

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君賜食必正席先嘗之
任啓元
同考試官教諭何　批〔發夫子敬君之容不事雕琢而〕
天然得體
考試官教諭吳　批〔詞簡意盡風骨儼然〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔調雅詞精〕
聖人承賜食而其禮周焉敬君之至也甚矣聖
===
人事君盡禮也一賜食而禮無不周非敬君之
至而何且夫人君有賜於臣即一食亦惠也人
臣事君以敬即拜賜亦禮也夫子之爲人臣也
其在朝廷固無往不敬矣至於承君之賜何如
蓋其道行於見可之時則奠食於朝者臣有常
數禮出乎公養之外則推食於下者君有特施
此蓋食頒君庖恐其餘也固不敢奉以薦先賜
由君命昭其寵也亦不敢遽以頒下夫子則明
惠方承於拜受而恭肅以就其位者自凜乎咫
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「君賜食，必正席先嘗之。」
任啓元
同考試官教諭何　批：〔發夫子敬君之容，不事雕琢，而〕天然得體。
考試官教諭吳　批：〔詞簡意盡，風骨儼然。〕
考試官教諭黎　批：〔調雅詞精。〕
聖人承賜食而其禮周焉，敬君之至也。甚矣，聖人事君盡禮也！一賜食而禮無不周，非敬君之至而何？
且夫人君有賜於臣，即一食亦惠也；人臣事君以敬，即拜賜亦禮也。夫子之爲人臣也，其在朝廷固無往不敬矣；至於承君之賜何如？
蓋其道行於見可之時，則奠食於朝者，臣有常數；禮出乎公養之外，則推食於下者，君有特施。此蓋食頒君庖，恐其餘也，固不敢奉以薦先；賜由君命，昭其寵也，亦不敢遽以頒下。夫子則明惠方承於拜受，而恭肅以就其位者，自凜乎咫
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"When the ruler bestowed cooked food upon him, he would inevitably straighten his mat and be the first to taste it."
Ren Qiyuan 任啓元
Associate Examiner Instructor He 何 comments: 〔He brings out the Master's demeanor in respecting his ruler; without resorting to artificial embellishment,〕 it is naturally fitting and proper.
Examiner Instructor Wu 吳 comments: 〔The words are concise, the meaning is fully expressed, and its vigor and character are dignified.〕
Examiner Instructor Li 黎 comments: 〔The tone is elegant and the diction refined.〕
When the Sage received a bestowal of cooked food, his observance of ritual was thorough in every respect—such was the utmost degree of his reverence for his ruler. Great indeed was the Sage's fulfillment of ritual in serving his ruler! In a single bestowal of food, there was no aspect of ritual left unattended—what was this if not the utmost reverence for his ruler?
Moreover, when a ruler bestows something upon a minister, even a single meal is an act of grace; when a minister serves his ruler with reverence, even bowing to receive a gift is a matter of ritual. When the Master served as a minister, at court there was indeed no occasion on which he was not reverent; what, then, of when he received a bestowal from his ruler?
Now, when his Way was practiced at a time he saw to be promising, for eating at court the minister had a regular stipend; when the courtesy went beyond public maintenance, in sharing his food with those below, the ruler made a special bestowal. Since this cooked food was distributed from the ruler's kitchen, lest it be leftover food, he certainly did not dare offer it in sacrifice to his ancestors; and since the gift came by the ruler's command, to manifest the favor shown him, neither did he dare hastily distribute it to his subordinates. As for the Master, just as the illustrious grace was received with a bow of acceptance, in reverently and solemnly taking his place on his mat, he naturally felt awe as though within a foot of…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
天之嚴殊既方接於登嘉而祇恪以飫其馨者
自翼乎對揚之度侍食先飯其在君所則然也
而食隆於晉錫此何賜也顧可忽耶對其賜即
對其君此身之不正不坐者蓋雖當夫退食之
頃而靡敢自寧矣變色而作其於盛饌則然也
而食分於鼎養此何品也顧可虛耶敬其君即
敬其食此心之不敢不飽者蓋愈謹於授餐之
際而罔敢或後矣斯則拜賜之節既已篤於尊
君而廣惠之仁復因之以逮下由是賜腥賜生
===
莫非推吾之敬以達吾仁孝之心耳夫子事君
之禮何其曲而中哉雖然夫子之於君賜如此
乎其恭也穆公亟餽子思何獨以僕僕爲勞乎
蓋國君養賢固自有道非所以語官守之義也
夫子仕有官職其於君食之微猶曲盡其禮如
此非萬世人臣之所當法與
齊明盛服非禮不動所以脩身也
何洛書
同考試官教諭陳　批　明暢典雅不落筌蹄文之佳
punctuated:
天之嚴；殊既方接於登嘉，而祇恪以飫其馨者，自翼乎對揚之度。侍食先飯，其在君所則然也；而食隆於晉錫，此何賜也，顧可忽耶？對其賜即對其君，此身之不正不坐者，蓋雖當夫退食之頃，而靡敢自寧矣。變色而作，其於盛饌則然也；而食分於鼎養，此何品也，顧可虛耶？敬其君即敬其食，此心之不敢不飽者，蓋愈謹於授餐之際，而罔敢或後矣。斯則拜賜之節，既已篤於尊君，而廣惠之仁，復因之以逮下。由是賜腥、賜生，莫非推吾之敬以達吾仁孝之心耳。夫子事君之禮，何其曲而中哉！雖然，夫子之於君賜，如此乎其恭也，穆公亟餽子思，何獨以僕僕爲勞乎？蓋國君養賢，固自有道，非所以語官守之義也。夫子仕有官職，其於君食之微，猶曲盡其禮如此，非萬世人臣之所當法與？

齊明盛服，非禮不動，所以脩身也。
何洛書
同考試官教諭陳　批：明暢典雅，不落筌蹄，文之佳
translation_en:
…the majesty of Heaven just a foot away; and just as this extraordinary grace is received as a fine offering, in reverently and attentively savoring its fragrance, he naturally maintains the respectful bearing of one responding to the ruler's favor. When attending the ruler at a meal, tasting the food first is what he did in the ruler's presence; yet when cooked food is generously bestowed upon him, what a gift this is—how could it be treated lightly? Facing the gift is just like facing the ruler himself; thus, his not sitting unless his posture and mat were straight meant that even at the moment of retiring for his meal, he never dared to be at ease with himself. Changing countenance and rising is what he did before a sumptuous feast; yet when food is shared from the ruler's own tripods, what a dish this is—how could it be received in vain? Revering the ruler is just like revering his food; thus, his mind not daring not to taste and eat his fill meant that he was all the more cautious at the moment the meal was presented, never daring to lag behind. In this way, the ritual of bowing to receive the gift was already deeply devoted to honoring the ruler, and the benevolence of extending favor could in turn reach those below. Consequently, whether the gift was raw meat or a live animal, it was nothing other than extending his own reverence to fulfill his heart of benevolence and filial piety. How intricate and yet unerringly proper were the rites by which the Master served his ruler! Even so, since the Master was so respectful toward the ruler's gifts, when Duke Mu repeatedly sent gifts of food to Zisi, why did Zisi alone consider the constant bowing a nuisance? This is because a ruler of a state naturally has a proper way to nourish the worthy, which is not to be discussed in the same terms as the duty of one holding an official post. The Master served in an official capacity, and even in so small a matter as food from the ruler, he thoroughly fulfilled the rites to such a degree—is this not what ministers for ten thousand generations ought to take as their model?

"To fast, to be pure, to wear full ceremonial dress, and to make no movement contrary to the rites: this is the way to cultivate the person."
He Luoshu 何洛書

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
者
考試官教諭吳　批〔氣和語莊雅有體認〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔腴潤明確〕
中庸言君身之脩一於敬而已矣夫敬者聖學
之要也一敬立而身無不脩矣茲非九經之首
務哉且夫天下之道本諸身吾身之德聚於敬
脩身而道立矣而脩之果何以哉彼心者身之
主也則齊明以潔其內而無貳無雜不失吾純
一之常中心無斯須之不敬焉服者身之章也
===
則盛服以飭其躬而有嚴有翼毋褻其尊之
體外貌無斯須之不敬焉又必致謹於念慮之
發而以禮制心一毫非禮之念不以之動於中
也祗慎於威儀之著而以禮治躬一毫非禮之
事不以之動於外也斯其內外交養而所以檢
束乎此身者既有以立之於中正之矩動靜不
違而所以防範乎此身者又有以約之於軌物
之閑聖敬日躋而德自臻於罔覺其所蘊之爲
天德之精者於是而豫其體矣敬脩可願而道
punctuated:
者。
考試官教諭吳批：〔氣和語莊，雅有體認。〕
考試官教諭黎批：〔腴潤明確。〕

《中庸》言君身之脩，一於敬而已矣。夫敬者，聖學之要也。一敬立而身無不脩矣，茲非九經之首務哉？且夫天下之道本諸身，吾身之德聚於敬。脩身而道立矣，而脩之果何以哉？彼心者，身之主也，則齊明以潔其內，而無貳無雜，不失吾純一之常，中心無斯須之不敬焉；服者，身之章也，則盛服以飭其躬，而有嚴有翼，毋褻其尊之體，外貌無斯須之不敬焉。又必致謹於念慮之發，而以禮制心，一毫非禮之念，不以之動於中也；祗慎於威儀之著，而以禮治躬，一毫非禮之事，不以之動於外也。斯其內外交養，而所以檢束乎此身者，既有以立之於中正之矩；動靜不違，而所以防範乎此身者，又有以約之於軌物之閑。聖敬日躋，而德自臻於罔覺，其所蘊之爲天德之精者，於是而豫其體矣；敬脩可願，而道
translation_en:
…one.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wu's comment: [Harmonious in spirit and dignified in expression; it shows refined personal insight.]
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Li's comment: [Rich, polished, clear, and precise.]

When the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of cultivating the ruler's person, it comes down solely to reverence. Indeed, reverence is the essential core of sagely learning. Once reverence is established, there is nothing in one's person that remains uncultivated—is this not the foremost task among the Nine Standard Rules (jiujing)? Furthermore, the Way of All under Heaven is rooted in the ruler's person, and the virtue of one's person is gathered in reverence. When the person is cultivated, the Way is established; yet by what means is it truly cultivated? The mind is the master of the person; thus one maintains fasting and purity to cleanse the interior, free of duplicity and admixture, never losing one's constant state of pure unity, so that within the mind there is not a moment's lack of reverence. Robes are the emblem of the person; thus one dons full attire to regulate the body, solemn and reverent, never profaning one's exalted station [?], so that in outward demeanor there is not a moment's lack of reverence. One must also exercise utmost caution at the stirrings of thoughts and intentions, regulating the mind through ritual propriety so that not the slightest improper thought is allowed to stir within; and one must be reverently careful in the manifestation of dignified bearing, governing the body through ritual propriety so that not the slightest improper act is allowed to stir without. Thus, with inner and outer mutually nourished, that by which this person is restrained is already established upon the standard of centrality and correctness; and with movement and stillness never departing from it, that by which this person is guarded is further bound within the bounds of regular norms. As sagely reverence daily ascends, virtue naturally reaches perfection imperceptibly, and that which is stored within as the essence of Heavenly virtue thereby has its substance prepared in advance; as one reverently cultivates what is desirable, the Way…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
自積於厥躬其所達之爲王道之大者於是而
涵其用矣吁以此脩身則身無不脩而以之用
人以之行政皆無施而不當矣尚何文武之政
之難舉乎抑斯言也帝王相傳之心法也精一
危微昉於唐虞而端本之化有自來矣然必有
緝煕而後可以言敬止必有睿聖而後可以言
皇極此明善所以爲誠身之要而學問思辨之
功夫丁盎諄諄焉故曰明君以務學爲急
民事不可緩也詩云晝爾于茅宵爾索綯
亟其乘屋其始播百穀
===
吳定
同考試官教授紀　批〔發明人重農之意婉曲詳盡而〕
考試官教諭吳　批〔氣充詞婉能發人所未發取〕
〔題意曜然〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔用意精深造語明瞥起繳處尤〕
之
〔爽剴緊切讀之惕然〕
大賢啓時君農事之當重必引詩以明之焉蓋
punctuated:
自積於厥躬，其所達之爲王道之大者，於是而涵其用矣。吁！以此脩身，則身無不脩，而以之用人、以之行政，皆無施而不當矣。尚何文武之政之難舉乎？抑斯言也，帝王相傳之心法也。精一危微昉於唐虞，而端本之化有自來矣。然必有緝煕而後可以言敬止，必有睿聖而後可以言皇極。此明善所以爲誠身之要，而學問思辨之功，夫丁盎諄諄焉。故曰：明君以務學爲急。
民事不可緩也。《詩》云：「晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。」
吳定
同考試官教授紀　批：〔發明人重農之意，婉曲詳盡，而題意曜然。〕
考試官教諭吳　批：〔氣充詞婉，能發人所未發，取之。〕
考試官教諭黎　批：〔用意精深，造語明瞥，起繳處尤爽剴緊切，讀之惕然。〕
大賢啓時君農事之當重，必引《詩》以明之焉。蓋
translation_en:
… naturally accumulates within his person, and what he extends outward as the greatness of the Kingly Way thereby encompasses its application. Ah! By cultivating one's person in this manner, there is nothing in the person left uncultivated; and in employing men and conducting government by means of it, there is nothing undertaken that is not fitting. How then could the governance of Kings Wen and Wu still be difficult to institute? Moreover, these words represent the method of the mind transmitted from one emperor and king to another. "Refinement and singleness," the "precarious and subtle," began with Tang Yao and Yu Shun, and the transformative influence of rectifying the root has had a long origin. Yet there must first be continuous bright illumination before one can speak of resting in reverence, and there must first be perspicacious sageliness before one can speak of the August Ultimate. This is why understanding goodness is the essential way to make the person sincere, and why the Master [Zisi] earnestly and repeatedly stressed the efforts of studying, inquiring, reflecting, and discriminating [? 夫丁盎]. Therefore it is said: An enlightened ruler regards devotion to learning as his urgent priority.

"The affairs of the people must not be delayed. The Book of Odes says: 'In the day go gather the reeds; in the night twist your ropes; get up quickly on the roofs; for soon you will begin to sow the hundred grains.'"

Wu Ding 吳定

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
農事國之本也徹諸詩而民之重農可見矣人
君顧可緩乎哉孟子以王道迪滕君而先之以
此若曰天之立君以爲民也君之奉天以子民
也君欲爲國盡於民事加之意乎是故經國之
始他務未遑也思民生之宜厚而汲汲於田功
之卽蒞政之初庶績未舉也思養道之宜先而
切切於力穡之圖時乎春則省乎耕焉勵東作
之勤不可以爲小人之事畧之矣時乎秋則省
乎斂焉督西成之務不可以爲農夫之憂忽之
矣若此者豈無所見而顧爲是以自勞哉蓋嘗
有徵於豳風之詩矣其曰晝爾于茅宵爾索綯
亟其乘屋其始播百穀卽其詩也繹其旨也備
物於蚕衣以亟乘屋之舉因農而急於工也執
功於歲晚聿興俶載之思因工而念乎農也三
時之逸不自知其逸取茅于晝急訖以爲來歲
之計豳民無一日不心乎農矣人君將善體民
心者烏可緩哉安居之樂不自知其樂索綯于
宵速成以先于耜之謀豳民無一時不心乎農
punctuated: 農事，國之本也。徹諸《詩》，而民之重農可見矣，人君顧可緩乎哉？孟子以王道迪滕君，而先之以此，若曰：天之立君，以爲民也；君之奉天，以子民也。君欲爲國，盡於民事加之意乎？是故經國之始，他務未遑也，思民生之宜厚，而汲汲於田功之卽；蒞政之初，庶績未舉也，思養道之宜先，而切切於力穡之圖。時乎春，則省乎耕焉，勵東作之勤，不可以爲小人之事畧之矣；時乎秋，則省乎斂焉，督西成之務，不可以爲農夫之憂忽之矣。若此者，豈無所見而顧爲是以自勞哉？蓋嘗有徵於《豳風》之詩矣。其曰：「晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。」卽其詩也，繹其旨也，備物於蚕衣，以亟乘屋之舉，因農而急於工也；執功於歲晚，聿興俶載之思，因工而念乎農也。三時之逸，不自知其逸，取茅于晝，急訖以爲來歲之計，豳民無一日不心乎農矣，人君將善體民心者，烏可緩哉？安居之樂，不自知其樂，索綯于宵，速成以先于耜之謀，豳民無一時不心乎農
translation_en:
…agricultural work is the foundation of the state. When one examines the Book of Odes (Shi), the weight that the people attach to agriculture becomes evident; how, then, could a ruler afford to be remiss? Mencius guided the ruler of Teng in the Kingly Way and began with this point, as if to say: "Heaven establishes the ruler for the sake of the people, and the ruler serves Heaven by treating the people as his children. If Your Majesty wishes to govern the state, why not devote your full attention [?] to the affairs of the people?"

Therefore, at the outset of ordering the state, before there is leisure for other tasks, one reflects that the people's livelihood ought to be enriched, and thus urgently attends to the work of the fields. At the beginning of assuming governance, before the various achievements have been initiated, one reflects that the way of nourishing the people ought to come first, and thus earnestly plans for diligent husbandry. When the season is spring, he inspects the plowing; encouraging the diligence of the spring work in the east, he cannot slight it as merely the business of petty men. When the season is autumn, he inspects the harvesting; supervising the tasks of the autumn completion in the west, he cannot neglect it as merely the concern of farmers.

In acting thus, how could he be without insight and yet trouble himself in this manner? Indeed, there is evidence for this in the ode of the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng). It says: "In the day go gather the cog-grass, and at night twist your ropes; haste to get up on the roofs, for soon we shall begin to sow the hundred grains." Taking this very ode and unfolding its meaning: preparing materials at the time of wrapping in winter clothes [?] in order to hasten the work of ascending the roofs is to hurry with construction work on account of agriculture; applying oneself to labor at the close of the year while rousing thoughts of beginning work in the southern acre is to keep agriculture in mind while engaged in construction work.

During the leisure after the three farming seasons, they do not consider themselves at ease: gathering cog-grass by day, they hurry to finish so as to plan for the coming year. Not a single day passes in which the people of Bin do not have their minds set on agriculture—how, then, could a ruler who wishes to sympathize well with the minds of the people afford to be remiss? In the pleasure of dwelling in peace, they do not consider themselves at pleasure: twisting ropes by night, they quickly complete them in advance of their plans to repair the plowshares. Not a single moment passes in which the people of Bin do not have their minds set on agriculture…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣人君將憂恤民隱者又可緩哉是知農者民
之命重農所以裕民也民者邦之本裕民所以
寧邦也君欲爲國其尚三復於斯抑農者帝王
傳心之要周以農事開國孟子於滕君惓惓致
意且引周公戒成王之詩以告之正欲之以王
道啓之以法祖也夫何井地之問雖少與其善
念而許子之說又從而惑之竟使孟子復古之
政托諸空言也

translation_en:
… How then can a ruler who wishes to show concern and compassion for the hidden hardships of the people afford to delay! From this we know that agriculture is the lifeblood of the people, and valuing agriculture is the means to enrich the people; the people are the foundation of the state, and enriching the people is the means to bring peace to the state. If Your Majesty wishes to govern the state, may you reflect upon this again and again! Moreover, agriculture is the essential mind-to-mind transmission of the emperors and kings. The Zhou dynasty founded its state upon agricultural pursuits. When Mencius earnestly expressed his thoughts to the ruler of Teng, even citing the poem with which the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng in order to instruct him, he precisely wished to guide [?] him with the Kingly Way and inspire him to model himself after his ancestors. Yet how regrettable that although his inquiry about the well-field system slightly aroused [?] his good intentions, the doctrines of Master Xu (Xu Xing 許行) subsequently deluded him, ultimately causing Mencius's governance for restoring antiquity to be consigned to empty words.

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
者其勢也而其相感者則機也物類之感旦有
然者而况於聖人乎今夫聖人統天德以作元
后而正位凝命躬膺乎曆數之傳握乾符以臨
兆民而乘龍御天弘敷其龍綏之化恭已無爲
雖無心於萬物之觀也然所存者神而天下之
心志一焉舉斯世之類相關者咸格其景從之
願嚮明而治若不期於萬物之從也然所過者
化而天下之耳目新焉舉斯世之性相同者悉
動其拱向之誠欽垂裳之度而戴之者有元后
===
之尊焉無一物而非其所怙冒則亦無一物而
不快覩其休也覲錫極之光而愛之者有父母
之親焉無一地而非其所涵育則亦無一地而
不對揚其盛也蓋聖人與天地合其德者也圓
於覆載之中未有不仰其生成之德者矣其與
聲氣水火之應不其異類而同機也哉與日月
合其明者也處於照臨之下未有不瞻其光輝
之盛者矣其與雲龍風虎之從不其異事而同
神也哉噫此九五之所以爲大人而爲人所利
punctuated: 者，其勢也；而其相感者，則機也。物類之感，旦有然者，而况於聖人乎？今夫聖人統天德以作元后，而正位凝命，躬膺乎曆數之傳；握乾符以臨兆民，而乘龍御天，弘敷其龍綏之化。恭已無爲，雖無心於萬物之觀也，然所存者神，而天下之心志一焉，舉斯世之類相關者，咸格其景從之願；嚮明而治，若不期於萬物之從也，然所過者化，而天下之耳目新焉，舉斯世之性相同者，悉動其拱向之誠。欽垂裳之度，而戴之者有元后之尊焉，無一物而非其所怙冒，則亦無一物而不快覩其休也；覲錫極之光，而愛之者有父母之親焉，無一地而非其所涵育，則亦無一地而不對揚其盛也。蓋聖人與天地合其德者也，圓於覆載之中，未有不仰其生成之德者矣，其與聲氣水火之應，不其異類而同機也哉？與日月合其明者也，處於照臨之下，未有不瞻其光輝之盛者矣，其與雲龍風虎之從，不其異事而同神也哉？噫！此九五之所以爲大人，而爲人所利
translation_en: … is a matter of their position; yet what makes them move and respond to one another is a subtle mechanism. If even the resonance among classes of things is such [reading 旦 as 且], how much more so with the sage! Now, the sage unifies the virtue of Heaven to act as the great sovereign; occupying the correct position and consolidating the Mandate, he personally receives the transmission of the Heaven-ordained succession. Holding the tally of Qian to rule over the millions of the people, he rides the dragons to drive through the heavens and broadly spreads the transforming influence of his寵綏 [reading 龍綏 as 寵綏, gracious pacification]. Reverent in himself and practicing non-action, although he has no deliberate intention of being beheld by the myriad things, yet what he preserves within is numinous, and the minds and wills of the world are unified by it; all in this world who are related in kind fulfill their wish to follow him like a shadow. Facing the light and governing, it is as though he does not expect the myriad things to follow him, yet wherever he passes, transformation takes place, and the ears and eyes of the world are renewed by it; all in this world who share the same nature are stirred in their sincerity to turn toward him in reverence. Revering the bearing of his垂裳 (hanging robes), those who look up to him honor him as the great sovereign; since there is not a single thing that is not sheltered and covered by him, there is likewise not a single thing that does not joyfully behold his blessings. Beholding the light of the supreme standard he bestows, those who love him feel the affection due to parents; since there is not a single place that is not nourished and nurtured by him, there is likewise not a single place that does not respond to and extol his flourishing virtue. Indeed, the sage is one who matches his virtue with Heaven and Earth; encircled [reading 圓 as 囿] within what they cover and support, there is none who does not look up to his virtue of generating and completing. Compared with the mutual response of sound, vital氣 (breath), water, and fire, are they not different in kind yet identical in their subtle mechanism? He is one who matches his brilliance with the sun and moon; dwelling beneath their shining gaze, there is none who does not gaze upon the abundance of his radiant splendor. Compared with clouds following the dragon and winds following the tiger, are they not different in affair yet identical in their numinous power? Ah! Is this not why the Nine in the Fifth Place is the Great Man, and why it is advantageous for people to…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
見也與抑此利見之聖人非他也仰體仁之君
子也故堯仁如天巍巍蕩蕩史臣紀其事而贊
之曰望之如日就之如雲德不可名而以仰望
於天下者形狀之則仁者其帝王之所以格天
致治者與故觀大人之利見取其體仁之功可
也
天地之大德曰生　王价
同考試官教諭何　批〔通篇一洗塵詞臨風三誦郎有〕
===

大傳發造化之蘊必指其生物者以見之也夫
天地以生物爲心者也觀其所生而天地無餘
蘊矣且夫參贊者聖人之能而天地者羣物之
祖聖人制易固皆原於天地矣天地之大何如
今夫天位乎上而無不覆幬孰不曰此天之大
也不知所以爲大者非徒以其職覆而已也地
punctuated:
見也與！抑此利見之聖人，非他也，仰體仁之君子也。故堯仁如天，巍巍蕩蕩，史臣紀其事而贊之曰：「望之如日，就之如雲。」德不可名，而以仰望於天下者形狀之，則仁者，其帝王之所以格天致治者與！故觀大人之利見，取其體仁之功可也。
天地之大德曰生。　王价

《大傳》發造化之蘊，必指其生物者以見之也。夫天地以生物爲心者也，觀其所生，而天地無餘蘊矣。且夫參贊者，聖人之能；而天地者，羣物之祖。聖人制《易》，固皆原於天地矣，天地之大何如？今夫天位乎上而無不覆幬，孰不曰「此天之大也」？不知所以爲大者，非徒以其職覆而已也。地
translation_en:
… advantageous to see! Moreover, this sage whom it is advantageous to see is none other than the noble man who embodies benevolence [? 仰 likely for 即]. Thus Yao's benevolence was like Heaven, towering and vast; the historian recorded his deeds and praised him, saying, "Looked upon from afar, he is like the sun; approached, he is like the clouds." Because his virtue could not be named, it was described in terms of how the world looked up to him. Is not benevolence, then, that whereby emperors and kings reach Heaven and bring about order? Therefore, in observing how it is advantageous to see the great man, one may simply take it from his achievement in embodying benevolence.

"The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving." — Wang Jie 王价
Associate Examiner, Instructor He 何 comments: [The entire essay washes away all dusty clichés. Reciting it thrice before the breeze, even if one had (? 郎有 for 即有)] any superficial airs, they could no longer intrude!
Examiner, Instructor Wu 吳 comments: [It elucidates the mind of Heaven and Earth in giving life to things—earnest, substantive, and worthy of recording.]
Examiner, Instructor Li 黎 comments: [The principles are clear and the diction harmonious (? 詞邕 for 詞暢)—the finest of essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes (Yi 易).]

When the Great Commentary (Dazhuan 大傳) reveals the inner depths of creative transformation, it necessarily points to its giving life to things in order to make it manifest. Now, Heaven and Earth take giving life to things as their mind; when one observes what they bring to life, nothing of the depths of Heaven and Earth remains hidden. Furthermore, participating in and assisting transformation is the capacity of the sage, whereas Heaven and Earth are the ancestors of the myriad things. When the sages fashioned the Book of Changes, it was indeed rooted entirely in Heaven and Earth. What, then, is the greatness of Heaven and Earth like? Now, Heaven is positioned above and shelters all without exception—who does not say, "This is the greatness of Heaven"? Yet they do not know that what makes it great is not merely its function of sheltering. Earth…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
位乎下而無不持載孰不曰此地之大也不知
其所以爲大者非徒以其職載而已也然天地
之大不可名所可名者德也故可以一言以盡
之曰生而已蓋其易簡交相爲用渾涵乎立命
之原凡天下之有性情者皆其所賦予也陰陽
互發其機默運乎太和之化凡天下之有形體
者皆其所發育也根柢乎一物之微而兼統乎
萬象之表無處非物則亦無一處而非其所生
也惟生以爲萬物之命則亦惟生以見天地之
心以此言天地不可以徵其德之大哉充周於
===
一息之間而流通乎萬世之遠無時非物則亦
無一時而非其所生也惟生以達造物之用則
亦惟生以觀天地之情以此言大德不可以盡
天地之妙哉夫天地之大如此故以此爲物象
之宜則卦爻於是乎立矣以此爲民用之通則
吉凶於是乎生矣信乎天地爲易書之原而聖
人與之合德也與雖然天地固以生物爲大德
矣然秋冬爲肅殺之令亦謂之生可乎蓋天地
punctuated: 位乎下，而無不持載，孰不曰「此地之大也」？不知其所以爲大者，非徒以其職載而已也。然天地之大不可名，所可名者德也。故可以一言以盡之曰：生而已。蓋其易簡交相爲用，渾涵乎立命之原，凡天下之有性情者，皆其所賦予也；陰陽互發其機，默運乎太和之化，凡天下之有形體者，皆其所發育也。根柢乎一物之微，而兼統乎萬象之表，無處非物，則亦無一處而非其所生也。惟生以爲萬物之命，則亦惟生以見天地之心。以此言天地，不可以徵其德之大哉？充周於一息之間，而流通乎萬世之遠，無時非物，則亦無一時而非其所生也。惟生以達造物之用，則亦惟生以觀天地之情。以此言大德，不可以盡天地之妙哉？夫天地之大如此，故以此爲物象之宜，則卦爻於是乎立矣；以此爲民用之通，則吉凶於是乎生矣。信乎天地爲《易》書之原，而聖人與之合德也與！雖然，天地固以生物爲大德矣，然秋冬爲肅殺之令，亦謂之生，可乎？蓋天地
translation_en: …is positioned below and upholds and supports everything without exception; who does not say, "This is the greatness of Earth"? Yet they do not know that what makes it great is not merely its function of supporting. However, the greatness of Heaven and Earth cannot be named; what can be named is their virtue. Therefore, it can be summed up in a single word: "life" and nothing more. Indeed, their ease and simplicity interact in mutual function, encompassing the source that establishes destiny, so that everything in the world possessing nature and disposition is endowed by them. Yin and yang mutually trigger their mechanisms, silently driving the transformations of supreme harmony, so that everything in the world possessing form and body is nourished and nurtured by them. Rooted in the subtlety of a single thing, yet encompassing all beyond the myriad phenomena—since there is no place without things, there is likewise no single place that is not brought into life by them. Because it is solely through life that the destiny of the myriad things is constituted, it is likewise solely through life that the mind of Heaven and Earth is revealed. Speaking of Heaven and Earth in this way, can one not verify the greatness of their virtue? Filling the span of a single breath, yet flowing through the distance of ten thousand generations—since there is no time without things, there is likewise no single moment that is not brought into life by them. Because it is solely through life that the function of the Creator of Things is fulfilled, it is likewise solely through life that the disposition of Heaven and Earth is observed. Speaking of great virtue in this way, can one not fathom the marvel of Heaven and Earth? Since the greatness of Heaven and Earth is such as this, taking it as the appropriateness of the images of things, the hexagrams and lines were thereby established; taking it as the free flow of the people's use, good fortune and misfortune were thereby generated. Truly, Heaven and Earth are the source of the Book of Changes (Yi), and the sages match them in virtue! Even so, Heaven and Earth certainly take the generation of things as their great virtue; yet autumn and winter bring the seasonal ordinances of stern withering—can this also be called life? Indeed, the Way of Heaven and Earth…

text:
之道不翕聚則不能發散而滅息者所以爲生
息之本以此見其生物之心無時不存雖肅殺
亦生也聖人仁覆天下而亦不廢刑威其亦法
天地以爲生者哉故曰何以守位曰仁

大臣述至治徵於有聲而因聲以保其治也蓋
聲音之道與政通也即歌之於民者而因以勸
之至治其有終乎大禹欲舜念盆之言蓋謂帝
王之致治也以養民爲善政尤以保泰爲成功
今府事庶於脩和則所以養民者既得其敘矣
其徵諸民情何如荷天地自然之利而涵濡於
punctuated:
之道，不翕聚則不能發散，而滅息者所以爲生息之本。以此見其生物之心，無時不存，雖肅殺亦生也。聖人仁覆天下，而亦不廢刑威，其亦法天地以爲生者哉！故曰：「何以守位？曰仁。」

書
「九敘惟歌，戒之用休，董之用威，勸之以九歌。」
宋惟俊
同考試官教諭陳　批〔體莊詞暢，三復誦之，有遺音。〕
吳高薦
考試官教諭吳　批〔究奏太平之歌者，可取。〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔精潔弘大，統歸韶樂，更見出人。〕

大臣述至治徵於有聲，而因聲以保其治也。蓋聲音之道與政通也。即歌之於民者，而因以勸之，至治其有終乎！大禹欲舜念益之言，蓋謂帝王之致治也，以養民爲善政，尤以保泰爲成功。今府事庶於脩和，則所以養民者，既得其敘矣。其徵諸民情何如？荷天地自然之利，而涵濡於
translation_en:
…of Heaven and Earth is such that if it does not gather and contract, it cannot disperse and expand, so that extinction and cessation serve as the very foundation of generation and growth. From this we see that its mind to generate things is never absent at any time; even the stern withering of autumn and winter is also generation. The sage covers all under Heaven with benevolence, yet does not abolish penal authority; does he not also model himself on Heaven and Earth in fostering life? Therefore it is said: "How does one guard the throne? Through benevolence."

Classic of Documents (Shu)
"When the nine services are all in order, they may be sung of. Admonish them with what is admirable, supervise them with majesty, and encourage them with the nine songs."
Song Weijun 宋惟俊
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen, comments: [The style is dignified and the phrasing fluent; reciting it three times over leaves a lingering resonance.]
Wu Gaojian 吳高薦
Examiner, Instructor Wu, comments: [One that thoroughly performs the songs of Great Peace; worthy of selection.]
Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: [Refined, pure, vast, and grand; bringing everything together into the Shao music shows even more how it surpasses others.]

The great minister recounts how supreme governance is attested in sound, and how by relying on those sounds that governance is preserved. For the way of sounds and music is connected with governance. If one takes what is sung among the people and uses it to encourage them, will supreme governance not be brought to a lasting conclusion? When the Great Yu wished Shun to bear in mind the words of Yi [reading 盆 as 益], he meant that when emperors and kings bring about order, they take nourishing the people as good governance, and even more do they take preserving prosperity as completed achievement. Now that the treasuries and affairs approach being well-regulated and harmonized, the means of nourishing the people have already attained their proper order. title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
覆載者皆歌詠以發其休被帝王博濟之仁而
沐浴於生成者咸揄揚以鳴其盛六府之脩歌
其所自脩洋洋乎擊壤之餘音也三事之和歌
其所自和渢渢乎康衢之遺響也斯蓋養民之
政安以順故聖世之民樂而歌所謂無虞者如
此不有以勸之則治其可常保乎故勤於九功
者必戒諭而休美之作其勤也然猶激之使慕
耳怠於九功者必董責而戒勉之懲其怠也然
猶督之使從耳又必據其歌詠太平之音以宣
===
諸節奏而日與斯民相鼓舞焉以心感心凡勸
於用休者至此其益勤矣本其揄揚太和之韻
以叶諸律呂而日與斯民相提撕焉以機觸機
凡惕於用威者至此其無怠矣必如是而後脩
者常脩和者常和而謂之儆戒無虞者此也帝
其念哉雖然聲以化民末也禹顧惓惓於歌勸
何蓋人心之動因聲以宣審樂之音可以知政
虞庭君臣賡歌以至閭里下民罔不謳歌頌德
和氣洋溢此樂之原也典於后夔而盡善盡美
punctuated: 覆載者，皆歌詠以發其休；被帝王博濟之仁，而沐浴於生成者，咸揄揚以鳴其盛。六府之脩，歌其所自脩，洋洋乎擊壤之餘音也；三事之和，歌其所自和，渢渢乎康衢之遺響也。斯蓋養民之政安以順，故聖世之民樂而歌，所謂無虞者如此。不有以勸之，則治其可常保乎？故勤於九功者，必戒諭而休美之，作其勤也，然猶激之使慕耳；怠於九功者，必董責而戒勉之，懲其怠也，然猶督之使從耳。又必據其歌詠太平之音，以宣諸節奏，而日與斯民相鼓舞焉。以心感心，凡勸於用休者，至此其益勤矣；本其揄揚太和之韻，以叶諸律呂，而日與斯民相提撕焉。以機觸機，凡惕於用威者，至此其無怠矣。必如是，而後脩者常脩，和者常和，而謂之儆戒無虞者此也。帝其念哉！雖然，聲以化民，末也，禹顧惓惓於歌勸，何？蓋人心之動，因聲以宣；審樂之音，可以知政。虞庭君臣賡歌，以至閭里下民，罔不謳歌頌德，和氣洋溢，此樂之原也。典於后夔，而盡善盡美，
translation_en: …the sheltering of heaven and supporting of earth all sing and chant to express its blessings; those who experience the universally aiding benevolence of emperors and kings and bathe in their life-giving and nurturing grace all extol and praise to proclaim its flourishing. In the regulation of the Six Treasuries, they sing of how they came to be regulated—how vast and overflowing, like the lingering notes of the "Beating the Clods" song! In the harmonization of the Three Affairs, they sing of how they came to be harmonized—how resonant and floating, like the surviving echoes of the "Highroad" ballad! This is because the governance that nourishes the people is peaceful and compliant; thus the people of a sagely age rejoice and sing. What is meant by "free from anxiety" is just like this. Yet if there is nothing wherewith to encourage them, how can good governance be permanently preserved? Therefore, those who are diligent in the Nine Merits must be admonished, instructed, and commended, so as to rouse their diligence—yet this is still merely stimulating them to feel aspiration. Those who are negligent in the Nine Merits must be supervised, reproved, and warned to exert themselves, so as to chastise their negligence—yet this is still merely compelling them to obey. One must also base oneself upon the sounds of their singing and chanting of Great Peace, setting them forth in rhythmic measures, and daily join with the people in mutually inspiring and rousing one another. Moving heart with heart, all who were encouraged through the use of commendation will at this point become even more diligent. Grounding oneself in the rhymes of their extolling of Supreme Harmony, harmonizing them with the pitch-pipes, one daily joins with the people in mutually awakening and reminding one another. Triggering impulse with impulse, all who were made wary through the use of awe will at this point have no negligence at all. Only when it is like this will what is regulated remain ever regulated, and what is harmonized remain ever harmonized; and what is called "being cautious and admonition-minded when free from anxiety" is precisely this. May the Sovereign bear it in mind! Even so, transforming the people through sound is a secondary matter; why then was Yu so earnestly attentive to encouraging them with songs? Because the movements of the human heart are expressed through sound, and by examining the tones of music, one can understand governance. In the court of Yu [Shun], sovereign and ministers exchanged songs in antiphony, and down to the common folk in the villages and lanes, there were none who did not sing ballads in praise of virtue. Harmonious vital energy overflowed everywhere—this was the origin of music. Directed by Sovereign Kui, its being perfectly good and perfectly beautiful…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
不有自哉後之陳詩而觀風者當執此以獻矣
小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕從罔匪正
人以旦夕承弼厥辟
闕廷訪
同考試官教諭陳　批〔造詞嚴整用意精深自獻之忠溢于言外高取〕
考試官教諭吳　批〔忠良正人詞多針線宜錄以式多士〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔切實不浮〕
===
聖世多賢臣而尤賴近臣以輔德爲甚矣近臣
有關于君德也忠良極盛而尤賴其承弼如此
斯文武之所以益聖與周王命伯冏之意蓋謂
君德不可不脩也是治之本也邇臣不可不慎
也是治之輔也不觀之文武乎蓋其聰明齊聖
德已罔愆矣維時之爲小臣大臣者精白以承
休各效夫致身之節靖恭以自獻共矢乎報國
之忱以迪彝教固五臣爲之夾輔也凡服勞王
家而惓惓于篤棐者皆三宅三俊之士以迪有
punctuated:
不有自哉！後之陳詩而觀風者，當執此以獻矣。

「小大之臣，咸懷忠良，其侍御僕從，罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。」
闕廷訪

考試官教諭吳　批〔忠良正人，詞多針線，宜錄以式多士。〕

聖世多賢臣，而尤賴近臣以輔德。爲甚矣，近臣有關于君德也！忠良極盛，而尤賴其承弼如此，斯文武之所以益聖與！周王命伯冏之意，蓋謂：君德不可不脩也，是治之本也；邇臣不可不慎也，是治之輔也。不觀之文、武乎？蓋其聰明齊聖，德已罔愆矣。維時之爲小臣、大臣者，精白以承休，各效夫致身之節；靖恭以自獻，共矢乎報國之忱。以迪彝教，固五臣爲之夾輔也；凡服勞王家而惓惓于篤棐者，皆三宅三俊之士。以迪有…
translation_en:
…does this not have its source? Those in later times who present poems to observe the customs should hold fast to this and offer it up.

"All his ministers, great and small, cherished loyalty and goodness; among his personal attendants and servants, there were none who were not upright men, morning and evening waiting on and assisting their sovereign." (Classic of History, Charge to Jiong)
By Que Tingfang 闕廷訪
Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: 〔The phrasing is rigorous and well-ordered, and the underlying intent is refined and profound. The loyalty of personal devotion overflows beyond the words; selected with a high ranking.〕
Examiner, Instructor Wu 吳 comments: 〔On "loyal and good" and "upright men," the phrasing has much fine stitching connecting the themes. It ought to be recorded as a model for the many scholars.〕
Examiner, Instructor Li 黎 comments: 〔Concrete and substantial, not superficial.〕

A sage age possesses many worthy ministers, yet it relies even more upon close attendants to assist in cultivating virtue. Profound indeed is the bearing that close attendants have upon the sovereign's virtue! Even when loyal and good ministers are at the height of abundance, still relying upon personal attendants for assistance in this manner—is this not whereby Kings Wen and Wu became ever more sagely? In giving his charge to Bo Jiong 伯冏, the King of Zhou meant to say: the sovereign's virtue cannot go uncultivated, for it is the root of governance; close attendants cannot be chosen without caution, for they are the auxiliaries of governance. Do we not see this in Kings Wen and Wu? Truly, in their intelligence, perspicacity, and sagely perfection, their virtue was already without fault. Those who served at that time as lesser and greater ministers maintained pure integrity to receive the royal grace, each devoting himself to the principle of offering his life in service; they practiced quiet reverence in presenting themselves, together swearing heartfelt sincerity in repaying the state. In guiding the constant instruction, there were indeed the five ministers acting as flanking supporters; all who labored for the royal house and were earnestly devoted to steadfast assistance were men fit for the three positions and men of the three grades of eminence.
