此其所不可爲者也又謂河勢浩猛欲分
punctuated: 急則廵隄，遇有決嚙，旋即乘時修築，毋使散漫。且新口未深，爲功尚易。如此，則不力專而河流急，縱有淤沙，隨即滾刷，可以無淤塞他徙之慮矣。黃河之水，□□險惡。未發，則水勢稍平而易行；既發，則水勢洶猛而莫測。迅流逆挽，跬步難前，遇險而傾，不可復救。今惟及水勢未發之前，令諸運艘必以春初渡江，夏初入閘。及至水發，則漕艘已過，不復冒險；況乘風直上，爲力更易。如此，則河勢平而舟行速，既出險阻，自能保全，可以無覆溺阻滯之慮矣。若謂海口沙墊，欲開濬以導之。夫下流不速，則上流必壅，導之誠是也。然海口沙洲，去海岸且二十里。今欲濬之，豈將以此二十里之廣，爲不足以洩黃河之水乎？如□□濬於中流，則中流未易以測其深也；況海□洲潮落即見，潮長即沒，縱欲開之，將何所施功乎？此其所不可爲者也。又謂河勢浩猛，欲分
translation_en: …and when the current is urgent, patrol the dikes. Whenever a breach or erosion occurs, immediately take advantage of the moment to repair and build it up, not allowing the water to spread unchecked. Moreover, when a new breach is not yet deep, the work of repairing it is still easy. In this way, the water's force [?] will be concentrated and the river current swift; even if there is silting sand, it will immediately be rolled away and scoured clean, and there need be no worry of the river silting up and shifting its course elsewhere. The waters of the Yellow River [are turbid and?] treacherous. Before the floods rise, the force of the water is relatively calm and easy to navigate; once the floods have risen, the water's force is surging, fierce, and unpredictable. Hauling upstream against a swift current, it is difficult to advance even a half-step; if a boat encounters danger and capsizes, it is beyond rescue. Now we should simply act before the floodwaters rise, ordering all grain-transport barges to cross the Yangtze in early spring and enter the canal locks in early summer. By the time the floodwaters rise, the tribute grain barges will have already passed through and will no longer have to brave the dangers; moreover, sailing straight up with the wind makes the effort even easier. In this way, the river will be calm and the boats will travel quickly; having cleared the perilous stretches, they will naturally be kept safe, and there need be no worry of capsizing, sinking, or delay. As for the claim that the river mouth at the sea is silted up and that we should excavate and dredge to guide the water through: now, if the lower reaches do not flow swiftly, the upper reaches will inevitably become backed up, so guiding it through is indeed right in principle. Yet the sandbars at the sea mouth are some twenty li from the seacoast. If we now wish to dredge there, could it be that we regard this twenty-li breadth as insufficient to discharge the waters of the Yellow River? And if [we wished to?] dredge in mid-channel, the depth of the mid-channel is not easy to fathom; moreover, the [sand]bars in the sea appear as soon as the tide ebbs and are submerged as soon as the tide rises—even if one wished to excavate them, where could the labor possibly be applied? This is something that cannot be done. Others say that the river's momentum is vast and fierce, and wish to divide…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
疏以殺之夫河流旣分則水勢自減疏之
誠是也然河流至入海且數百里今欲疏
之其能於此數百里之間別爲一入海之
道乎如欲分匯於他澤則何□□棄以居
此水也況河水勢專則速而利力分則漫
而淤縱欲分之能使其不淤乎此其所不
必爲者也蓋嘗卽黃河之勢而統觀之古
之黃河自西而東自東而卽北其取道也
稍近今則自西而東自東而北而又東而
===
南其取道也視昔又遠矣古之黃河河自
爲河淮自爲淮其合流也尚少今則河入
於汴汴入於泗泗入於沂而同會於淮其
合流也視昔益多矣故以今日之河較之
前代則其治之爲尤急以今日之治河較
之前代之治則其治之爲尤難□□昔人謂
昔之治河止去其害今之治河兼資其利
故難愚則謂昔之治河止去其害今之治
河兼資其利故易蓋於治河之中寓通漕
punctuated:
疏以殺之。夫河流旣分，則水勢自減，疏之誠是也。然河流至入海且數百里，今欲疏之，其能於此數百里之間別爲一入海之道乎？如欲分匯於他澤，則何□□棄以居此水也？況河水勢專則速而利，力分則漫而淤；縱欲分之，能使其不淤乎？此其所不必爲者也。

蓋嘗卽黃河之勢而統觀之：古之黃河自西而東，自東而卽北，其取道也稍近；今則自西而東，自東而北，而又東而南，其取道也視昔又遠矣。古之黃河，河自爲河，淮自爲淮，其合流也尚少；今則河入於汴，汴入於泗，泗入於沂，而同會於淮，其合流也視昔益多矣。故以今日之河較之前代，則其治之爲尤急；以今日之治河較之前代之治，則其治之爲尤難。□□昔人謂昔之治河止去其害，今之治河兼資其利，故難；愚則謂昔之治河止去其害，今之治河兼資其利，故易。蓋於治河之中寓通漕
translation_en:
…and dredge diversion channels to weaken its force. Now, once the river's flow is divided, the force of the water naturally diminishes, so dredging channels to divert it is indeed right. Yet from the river's main course to where it enters the sea is several hundred li; if we wish to dredge diversion channels now, could we possibly create another separate route to the sea across these several hundred li? And if we wished to divert and gather the water into other marshes, what [land could be?] abandoned to hold this water? Moreover, when the Yellow River's current is concentrated, it flows swiftly and smoothly; when its force is divided, it spreads out and silts up. Even if we wished to divide it, could we prevent it from silting up? This is what does not need to be done.

Indeed, if we examine the overall course and configuration of the Yellow River as a whole: in antiquity, the Yellow River flowed from west to east, and from east immediately turned north, taking a relatively short route; today, however, it flows from west to east, from east to north, and then east and south again, taking a route much longer than in the past. In antiquity, the Yellow River was the Yellow River and the Huai River was the Huai River, and their confluences were still few; today, however, the Yellow River enters the Bian River, the Bian enters the Si River, the Si enters the Yi River, and together they converge into the Huai River, so its confluences are much more numerous than in the past. Therefore, comparing the river of today with that of former dynasties, controlling it is even more urgent; and comparing river control today with that of former dynasties, controlling it is even more difficult. [Yet whereas?] people of the past said that river control in former times merely removed its harm, while river control today also relies on its benefit and is therefore difficult, I would say that because river control in former times merely removed its harm, while river control today also relies on its benefit, it is therefore easy. For by embedding the method of keeping the grain transport canal open within the work of river control…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之法是治河即所以治漕害去而利即存
矣不然則河自河而漕自漕將奔命之不
暇矣昔人謂復黃河已棄之故道也黃患
則謂復黃河新淤之故道也□□淤沙新
集而易刷故道得水而可衝則引水即可
以衝沙沙去而河即復矣不然則舍其故
而新是謀將徒勞而無益矣彼賈讓之三
策若放大河以入渤海多漕渠以分水勢
皆今日之所不可行者惟繕完故隄增卑
===
倍薄彼之所謂下策乃今之所謂長策也
賈魯之三法若釃河流而因導之抑河暴
而因扼之皆今日之所不必行者惟去河
之淤因而深之彼之所謂濬法乃今之所
謂要法也雖然河在徐邳經流未久夾河
之隄築基實土之上苟能慎□□足制水
若夫中州之境則久被河患地積浮沙
隨水嚙頃刻數十丈隄面猶存而其下空
洞平沉矣故徐邳河患土足制之而中州
punctuated: 之法，是治河即所以治漕，害去而利即存矣。不然，則河自河而漕自漕，將奔命之不暇矣。昔人謂：「復黃河已棄之故道也，難。」愚則謂：「復黃河新淤之故道也，□□。」淤沙新集而易刷，故道得水而可衝，則引水即可以衝沙，沙去而河即復矣。不然，則舍其故而新是謀，將徒勞而無益矣。彼賈讓之三策，若放大河以入渤海，多漕渠以分水勢，皆今日之所不可行者；惟繕完故隄，增卑倍薄，彼之所謂下策，乃今之所謂長策也。賈魯之三法，若釃河流而因導之，抑河暴而因扼之，皆今日之所不必行者；惟去河之淤，因而深之，彼之所謂濬法，乃今之所謂要法也。雖然，河在徐、邳，經流未久，夾河之隄，築基實土之上，苟能慎□□足制水；若夫中州之境，則久被河患，地積浮沙，隨水嚙，頃刻數十丈，隄面猶存而其下空洞平沉矣。故徐、邳河患，土足制之，而中州
translation_en: … the method of [maintaining the grain transport canal]; thus, controlling the Yellow River is itself the means of managing the grain transport, so that once the harm is removed, the benefit is automatically preserved. Otherwise, the River and the canal would be treated as separate matters, and one would be left rushing about in exhaustion with no time to spare. Men of the past said that restoring a long-abandoned old course of the Yellow River is difficult [reading 黃患 as 難,愚]; I, however, say that restoring a newly silted old course of the Yellow River is [easy] [?]. Because the silted sand has only recently accumulated, it is easy to scour away, and once the old channel receives water, it can be flushed out; thus, simply diverting the water in will suffice to flush away the sand, and when the sand is gone, the River is restored. Otherwise, to abandon the old channel and plan for a new one would be fruitless labor to no avail. As for the three strategies of Jia Rang 賈讓—such as releasing the great River to enter the Bohai Sea, or digging multiple transport canals to divide the force of the water—none of these can be put into practice today; only repairing and completing the old dikes, heightening the low sections and doubling the thin ones, which he called the lowest strategy, is what today we call the superior strategy. As for the three methods of Jia Lu 賈魯—such as dividing the River's current in order to guide it, or suppressing the River's violence in order to choke it back—none of these need be put into practice today; only removing the River's silt and thereby deepening it, which he called the method of dredging, is what today we call the essential method. Even so, in Xuzhou 徐州 and Pizhou 邳州 the River has not flowed through for long, and the dikes flanking the River have their foundations built upon solid earth; if one can carefully [maintain them, they are] [?] sufficient to control the water. As for the territory of Henan (Zhongzhou 中州), however, it has long suffered from the disasters of the River, and the ground is piled with loose, shifting sand; as the water gnaws at it, dozens of zhang collapse in an instant, so that while the surface of the dike still remains, underneath it is hollowed out and sinks flat. Therefore, against the River's threat in Xuzhou and Pizhou, earth alone is sufficient to control it, whereas in Henan…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
則非聯匝埽不可禦有此其工力之當借
者也河在徐邳運道所經沿河之職皆爲
漕艘而設所當協濟不可獨累若夫中州
之境則冬被河患民不聊生河決歲溢計
費數千金自繕不暇而無暇爲人防捍矣
故徐邳之河役諸省當濟之而中州則僅
可自給不能濟人此其經費之當計者也
嗚呼下流緊束則上流之勢可虞徐河既
狹則汴河難消下而虞考上而陽蘭皆可
===
慮也急處既防則緩處之防當豫汴河若
溢則開河被侵北而張秋南而曹單皆可
憂也則夫節夫役以存不盡之力計財費
以待不時之需特挑濬以保不毁之業治
遥隄以備不虞之患嚴守哨以防踈潰之
災平稍舒以抑侵耗之弊而□□退灘以
贍失業之民蠲租課以撫流移之衆□裨
國家之大計下紓生民之隱憂今日之所當
豫圖者也當事者其毋以中州河患之稍
punctuated: 則非聯匝埽不可禦有，此其工力之當借者也。河在徐、邳，運道所經，沿河之職皆爲漕艘而設，所當協濟，不可獨累；若夫中州之境，則冬被河患，民不聊生，河決歲溢，計費數千金，自繕不暇，而無暇爲人防捍矣。故徐、邳之河役，諸省當濟之，而中州則僅可自給，不能濟人，此其經費之當計者也。嗚呼！下流緊束，則上流之勢可虞，徐河既狹，則汴河難消，下而虞、考，上而陽、蘭，皆可慮也；急處既防，則緩處之防當豫，汴河若溢，則開河被侵，北而張秋，南而曹、單，皆可憂也。則夫節夫役以存不盡之力，計財費以待不時之需，特挑濬以保不毁之業，治遥隄以備不虞之患，嚴守哨以防踈潰之災，平稍舒以抑侵耗之弊，而□□退灘以贍失業之民，蠲租課以撫流移之衆，□裨國家之大計，下紓生民之隱憂，今日之所當豫圖者也。當事者其毋以中州河患之稍
translation_en:
… whereas in the Central Plain (Henan), the river cannot be held back without interlocking fascines [?]; this is why labor must be spared or borrowed. Where the Yellow River passes through Xuzhou 徐州 and Pizhou 邳州, it is the route of the Grand Canal, and the official posts along the river are all established for the grain transport fleet; thus they ought to receive joint financial assistance and should not be burdened alone. As for the territory of the Central Plain, it has long [reading 久 for 冬] suffered from river disasters and the people have no means of livelihood. The river breaches and overflows every year, costing thousands of taels of silver; the province scarcely has the capacity to repair its own defenses, let alone defend others. Therefore, the river corvée in Xuzhou and Pizhou should be subsidized by the various provinces, whereas the Central Plain can barely support itself and cannot subsidize others; this is how the expenditures ought to be calculated.

Alas! When the lower reaches are tightly constricted, the momentum in the upper reaches is cause for alarm. Since the river at Xuzhou is narrow, the river at Bian 汴 (Kaifeng) is difficult to drain; downstream in Yucheng 虞城 and Kaocheng 考城, and upstream in Yangwu 陽武 andanyang 蘭陽, all are cause for concern. Once the urgent points are defended, precautions must be taken in advance for the less urgent points. If the river at Bian overflows, the Huitong Canal (Kaihe 開河) will be encroached upon; Zhangqiu 張秋 to the north, and Caozhou 曹州 and Shanxian 單縣 to the south, will all be cause for worry. Therefore, economizing on corvée labor to preserve inexhaustible strength, calculating financial expenditures to meet unexpected needs, carrying out timely [reading 時 for 特] dredging to preserve an indestructible enterprise, building distant dikes to prepare against unforeseen disasters, strictly maintaining guard posts to prevent the calamity of negligent breaches, leveling reed-bundle levies [?; 平稍舒] to curb the abuses of embezzlement and waste, [granting?] receded滩涂 (alluvial flats) to support people who have lost their livelihoods, and remitting land taxes and levies to soothe the displaced multitudes—so as to benefit the grand plans of the state above, and relieve the hidden sorrows of the people below—these are what ought to be planned for in advance today. Let those in charge of affairs not take the slight… [of river disasters in the Central Plain as an excuse to shirk their responsibility!]

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
緩爲可諉哉
第五問
李復初
同考試官教授高　批〔今設問者先論將每以之才爲請蓋漢之任之未盡也子援古證今切中時弊或可採之而禦干城矣〕
考試官教諭吳　批〔膽而切辨而裁論將無踰子矣〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔論將獨歸以忠是知大體者〕
執事發策首論將才而因及選將任將之
術其思患豫防先事注意甚遠慮也愚生
請先舉將才之實而後及選之任之之術
===
可乎夫自古介冑之士所以克敵樹勳以
垂名竹帛者豈惟其才致然哉竭力盡能
心之忠爲之也夫將者國之幹而忠則幹
國之本才則所以濟之者也古今論兵法
者皆祖太公其言曰勇仁智信忠夫其列
勇仁智信而歸之于忠彼其意固欲使後
之爲將者以心事君不徒以才事君也夫
惟其心之主于忠也而後其勇也非剛愎
punctuated:
緩爲可諉哉！

第五問
李復初
同考試官教授高　批〔今設問者先論將，每以乏才爲請，蓋漢之任之未盡也。子援古證今，切中時弊，或可採之而禦干城矣。〕
考試官教諭吳　批〔贍而切，辨而裁，論將無踰子矣。〕
考試官教諭黎　批〔論將獨歸以忠，是知大體者。〕

執事發策，首論將才，而因及選將、任將之術，其思患豫防、先事注意，甚遠慮也。愚生請先舉將才之實，而後及選之、任之之術，可乎？夫自古介冑之士，所以克敵樹勳，以垂名竹帛者，豈惟其才致然哉？竭力盡能，心之忠爲之也。夫將者，國之幹；而忠，則幹國之本；才，則所以濟之者也。古今論兵法者，皆祖太公。其言曰：「勇、仁、智、信、忠。」夫其列勇、仁、智、信而歸之于忠，彼其意固欲使後之爲將者，以心事君，不徒以才事君也。夫惟其心之主于忠也，而後其勇也非剛愎，
translation_en:
…has abated slightly as an excuse to shirk their responsibility!

Fifth Policy Question
Li Fuchu 李復初
Comment by Associate Examiner Confucian School Instructor Gao 高: [Nowadays, those who pose questions first discuss generals and constantly lament a lack of talent [reading 以之才 as 以乏才?]; this is because in selecting and employing them [reading 漢之 as 選之?], we have not yet done everything required. You cite antiquity to verify the present and hit squarely on the ills of the age; perhaps one could adopt your views to defend the bulwarks of the state.]
Comment by Examiner Confucian School Instructor Wu 吳: [Rich yet incisive, analytical yet judicious—in discussing generals, none surpasses you.]
Comment by Examiner Confucian School Instructor Li 黎: [In discussing generals, you alone trace everything back to loyalty; you are one who understands the fundamental principles.]

Your Excellency, in posing this policy question, first discusses the talent of generals and thereby extends to the methods of selecting and employing generals; such forethought to guard against disaster and attention paid before events occur represent very far-sighted deliberation. May this ignorant student beg to first set forth the reality of martial talent, and afterward address the methods of selecting and employing them? Since antiquity, the reason armored warriors have been able to vanquish enemies, establish merit, and hand down their names on bamboo and silk—how could it be brought about merely by their talent? It is achieved by exhausting their strength and doing their utmost out of the loyalty of their hearts. Now, a general is the mainstay of the state; loyalty is the root of being the mainstay of the state, while talent is the means by which to bring it to fruition. Past and present, all who discuss the art of war take the Grand Duke (Taigong 太公) as their founder. His words say: "Courage, benevolence, wisdom, trustworthiness, and loyalty." By listing courage, benevolence, wisdom, and trustworthiness and culminating in loyalty, his intention was assuredly to cause those of later times who serve as generals to serve their ruler with their hearts, and not merely to serve their ruler with their talent. Only when one's heart is governed by loyalty will one's courage not be obstinate headstrongness,…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
其仁也非市恩其智也非詭譎其信也非
私約故勇加于天下而莫不威仁施于天
下而莫不愛智運于天下而莫不服信結
于天下而莫不用情其在上則孚于君而
無所疑其在下則孚于民而無所貳其在
當時則社稷賴其安其在後世則旂常行
其慶古之賢將所以德備于身功昭于國
者由此其選也孫武之論將則曰仁智信
勇嚴夫不曰忠而曰嚴彼徒恃法令以爲
===
整肅之具而不本之于心以爲報國安民
之基故其用之僅足以定霸而視王者鷹
揚之佐則有間矣吳起之論將則曰理備
果戒約夫不曰忠而曰約彼徒恃政務以
爲應敵之資而不根之于德以爲尊主庇
民之本故其用之僅足以取勝而視王者
神武之師則更遠矣夫其曰勇仁智信而
本之于忠者此將德也智仁信勇而加之
以嚴與夫理果戒備約者此將才也才備
punctuated: 其仁也非市恩，其智也非詭譎，其信也非私約。故勇加于天下而莫不威，仁施于天下而莫不愛，智運于天下而莫不服，信結于天下而莫不用情。其在上則孚于君而無所疑，其在下則孚于民而無所貳，其在當時則社稷賴其安，其在後世則旂常行其慶。古之賢將所以德備于身、功昭于國者，由此其選也。孫武之論將則曰：「仁、智、信、勇、嚴。」夫不曰忠而曰嚴，彼徒恃法令以爲整肅之具，而不本之于心以爲報國安民之基。故其用之僅足以定霸，而視王者鷹揚之佐則有間矣。吳起之論將則曰：「理、備、果、戒、約。」夫不曰忠而曰約，彼徒恃政務以爲應敵之資，而不根之于德以爲尊主庇民之本。故其用之僅足以取勝，而視王者神武之師則更遠矣。夫其曰勇、仁、智、信而本之于忠者，此將德也；智、仁、信、勇而加之以嚴，與夫理、果、戒、備、約者，此將才也。才備
translation_en:
…his benevolence is not currying favor, his wisdom is not deceitfulness, and his trustworthiness is not private pact-making. Therefore, when his courage is applied to the realm, none fail to be awed; when his benevolence is extended to the realm, none fail to feel affection; when his wisdom is exercised throughout the realm, none fail to submit; and when his trustworthiness binds the realm, none fail to devote their true feelings. Above, he inspires confidence in the ruler without any suspicion; below, he inspires confidence in the people without any duplicity. In his own time, the altars of soil and grain rely on him for peace; in later generations, the royal banners and ceremonial robes carry forward the blessings of his deeds. That the worthy generals of antiquity perfected virtue in their persons and made their achievements illustrious in the state was because they came from this kind of selection.

When Sun Wu 孫武 discussed generals, he said: "Benevolence, wisdom, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness." Now, by not speaking of loyalty and speaking instead of strictness, he merely relied on laws and ordinances as instruments for enforcing discipline, rather than rooting them in the mind as the foundation for repaying the state and pacifying the people. Therefore, when put to use, it was barely sufficient to establish hegemony, and compared to the hawk-like aides of a true king, there was a gulf between them.

When Wu Qi 吳起 discussed generals, he said: "Order, preparedness, decisiveness, vigilance, and simplicity." Now, by not speaking of loyalty and speaking instead of simplicity, he merely relied on administrative affairs as resources for responding to the enemy, rather than rooting them in virtue as the foundation for honoring the ruler and sheltering the people. Therefore, when put to use, it was barely sufficient to snatch victory, and compared to the divinely martial armies of a true king, it was further still.

Now, speaking of courage, benevolence, wisdom, and trustworthiness while rooting them in loyalty—this is the virtue of a general. Speaking of wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, and courage while adding strictness to them, along with order, decisiveness, vigilance, preparedness, and simplicity—this is the talent of a general. When talent is complete…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
而德亦備焉者蘇洵所謂賢將也周之方
叔召虎漢之寇恂馮異唐之李靖郭子儀
宋之曹彬岳飛是也此社稷之將也不備
而德不及焉者蘇洵所謂才將也秦之白
起王翦漢之英布彭越唐之薛萬徹侯君
集宋之党進楊業是也此忠雖未至而才
足以運之者也此封疆之將也故得千兵
易得一將難將而能也則兵卒皆可起敵
矣得才將十不如得賢將一將而賢也則
===
才者皆為我用矣然其選之也貴豫是故
探之窮居以觀其養較之騎射以觀其藝
詢之籌策以觀其謀試之政事以觀其能
激之以怒以觀其量醉之以酒以觀其度
內舉則不避親外舉則不避讎繁舉則不
避于夷狄盜賊以此而豫儲之則國家有
虎豹在山之勢以此而授用之則戎旅有
熊羆不二之臣何者其所以選之者豫也
然韓信楚亡卒也高帝一見拜為大將而
punctuated: 而德亦備焉者，蘇洵所謂賢將也。周之方叔、召虎，漢之寇恂、馮異，唐之李靖、郭子儀，宋之曹彬、岳飛是也，此社稷之將也。不備而德不及焉者，蘇洵所謂才將也。秦之白起、王翦，漢之英布、彭越，唐之薛萬徹、侯君集，宋之党進、楊業是也。此忠雖未至，而才足以運之者也，此封疆之將也。故得千兵易，得一將難；將而能也，則兵卒皆可起敵矣。得才將十，不如得賢將一；將而賢也，則才者皆為我用矣。然其選之也貴豫。是故探之窮居以觀其養，較之騎射以觀其藝，詢之籌策以觀其謀，試之政事以觀其能，激之以怒以觀其量，醉之以酒以觀其度。內舉則不避親，外舉則不避讎，繁舉則不避于夷狄、盜賊。以此而豫儲之，則國家有虎豹在山之勢；以此而授用之，則戎旅有熊羆不二之臣。何者？其所以選之者豫也。然韓信，楚亡卒也，高帝一見拜為大將，而
translation_en: … and whose virtue is also complete are what Su Xun 蘇洵 called "worthy generals" (xianjiang 賢將). Such were Fang Shu 方叔 and Shao Hu 召虎 of the Zhou, Kou Xun 寇恂 and Feng Yi 馮異 of the Han, Li Jing 李靖 and Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 of the Tang, and Cao Bin 曹彬 and Yue Fei 岳飛 of the Song; these are generals of the state altars (sheji zhi jiang 社稷之將). Those who are not complete and whose virtue falls short are what Su Xun called "talented generals" (caijiang 才將). Such were Bai Qi 白起 and Wang Jian 王翦 of the Qin, Ying Bu 英布 and Peng Yue 彭越 of the Han, Xue Wanche 薛萬徹 and Hou Junji 侯君集 of the Tang, and Dang Jin 党進 and Yang Ye 楊業 of the Song. In these men, although their loyalty has not reached the highest standard, their talent is sufficient to direct affairs; these are generals of the frontiers (fengjiang zhi jiang 封疆之將). Therefore, to obtain a thousand soldiers is easy, but to obtain a single general is difficult; if the general is capable, then the rank-and-file soldiers can all rise to face the enemy. To obtain ten talented generals is not as good as obtaining one worthy general; if the general is worthy, then the talented ones will all be at our disposal. Yet in selecting them, the crucial thing is preparation in advance. For this reason, one seeks them out in humble obscurity to observe their self-cultivation, tests them in horsemanship and archery to observe their martial skills, consults them on planning and strategy to observe their resourcefulness, tries them in administrative affairs to observe their ability, provokes them to anger to observe their forbearance, and intoxicates them with wine to observe their composure. In recommending from within, one does not shy away from relatives; in recommending from without, one does not shy away from personal enemies; in recommending broadly, one does not shy away even from foreign tribesmen or bandits. When they are stored up in advance in this manner, the state possesses the daunting posture of tigers and leopards in the mountains; when they are commissioned and employed in this manner, the armies possess fiercely loyal ministers of the caliber of bears and grisly bears. Why is this? Because the means by which they were selected were prepared in advance. Yet Han Xin 韓信 was a runaway soldier from Chu, whom Emperor Gao 高帝 at first sight appointed Grand General (dajiang 大將), and…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
卒以滅項衛青主家奴也武帝一見擢爲
將軍而卒以敗胡此二將者非有儲選之
素也二君用之皆能成功今之選將者豈
能拔士于行伍乎世胄廷蓮于簪纓卽行
伍有人焉弗能振也其能取人于奴隸乎
紈袴競耀于戎行卽奴隸有人焉將自廢
也斯則雖有淮陰長平弗能用也選將之
道其猶有未盡乎其任之也貴專是故寵
之爵祿以尊其位予之事權以盡其才推
===
之腹心以安其志假之體貌以壯其勢寬
之文法以任其用專之號令以肅其威借
之誅賞以重其令君命可以不受進退可
以自由用舍予奪可以自制以此而結士
則愛卒甚于愛子以此而赴鬬則畏將甚
于畏敵何者其所以任之者專也若李牧
北邊將也邊市租稅皆入幕府牧日饗士
而後用之卒以破胡虞詡武都長也攻劫
傷盜皆在募科詡旣得士而後進之卒以
punctuated: 卒以滅項；衛青，主家奴也，武帝一見，擢爲將軍，而卒以敗胡。此二將者，非有儲選之素也，二君用之，皆能成功。今之選將者，豈能拔士于行伍乎？世胄廷蓮于簪纓，卽行伍有人焉，弗能振也；其能取人于奴隸乎？紈袴競耀于戎行，卽奴隸有人焉，將自廢也。斯則雖有淮陰、長平，弗能用也，選將之道，其猶有未盡乎？其任之也貴專。是故寵之爵祿以尊其位，予之事權以盡其才，推之腹心以安其志，假之體貌以壯其勢，寬之文法以任其用，專之號令以肅其威，借之誅賞以重其令。君命可以不受，進退可以自由，用舍予奪可以自制。以此而結士，則愛卒甚于愛子；以此而赴鬬，則畏將甚于畏敵。何者？其所以任之者專也。若李牧，北邊將也，邊市租稅皆入幕府，牧日饗士而後用之，卒以破胡；虞詡，武都長也，攻劫傷盜皆在募科，詡旣得士而後進之，卒以
translation_en:
… ultimately destroyed Xiang Yu. Wei Qing 衛青 was a household slave of a princess; when Emperor Wu 武帝 saw him once, he promoted him to General, and he ultimately defeated the northern nomads. These two generals had not been previously reserved or selected, yet when the two rulers employed them, both were able to achieve success. Can those who select generals today promote men from the ranks and files? Hereditary scions succeed one another [?] in official caps and tassels; even if there are capable men in the ranks and files, they cannot rise up. Can they take men from among slaves and servants? Dandies in fine silks vie for glory in the military ranks; even if there are capable men among slaves and servants, they will abandon themselves to obscurity. Thus, even if there were a Marquis of Huaiyin 淮陰 [Han Xin] or a Marquis of Changping 長平 [Wei Qing], we could not employ them. Has the way of selecting generals still not been fully realized?

In employing them, what is valued is giving them exclusive authority. Therefore, honor them with noble ranks and emoluments to elevate their position; grant them operational authority to let them exhaust their talents; extend to them your heartfelt trust to set their minds at ease; accord them ceremonial courtesy to strengthen their prestige; relax the legal strictures upon them to give them free rein in their actions; make their commands exclusive to render their authority awe-inspiring; and lend them the power of execution and reward to give weight to their orders. There are sovereign commands they need not accept; advancing and retreating can be at their own discretion; employing and dismissing, giving and taking away, can be under their own control. When they bind the soldiers to themselves in this manner, the soldiers will love them more than a loving father loves his sons [or: they will love their soldiers more than their own sons]; when they go into battle in this manner, the soldiers will fear their general more than they fear the enemy. Why is this? Because the authority with which they are entrusted is exclusive.

For instance, Li Mu 李牧 was a general on the northern frontier; the revenues and taxes of the frontier markets all went into his headquarters treasury, and Mu feasted his men daily before putting them to use, ultimately routing the northern nomads. Yu Xu 虞詡 was the governor of Wudu 武都; bandits guilty of assault, robbery, and mayhem were all included in his recruitment categories, and once Xu had obtained such men, he advanced them into battle, ultimately…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
定羗此二將者皆出規格之外也二君假
之卒能樹績今之任將者能縱其錢穀而
不較乎用一財焉册籍少錯文法繩之矣
其何以養士耶能任其召募而不計乎用
一人焉來歷少誤勘核隨之矣其何以得
士耶斯則雖遇李牧虞詡弗能展也任將
之道其猶有未盡乎方今
皇上當大德受命之初正
聖作物覩之會薄海內外罔不臣服雖俺荅素
===
雄漠北亦歸心輸款奉
貢稱臣四海無虞休哉盛矣然狼子野心非
我族類窺覘虛實無日無之則除戎器戒
不虞固
今日之當務而選將材備任用尤
今日之所當豫圖者也邇者
聖謨加恤
廟議協心分
遣大臣巡行各邊飭諸將閱戎行覸城堡備
punctuated:
定羗。此二將者，皆出規格之外也；二君假之，卒能樹績。今之任將者，能縱其錢穀而不較乎？用一財焉，册籍少錯，文法繩之矣，其何以養士耶？能任其召募而不計乎？用一人焉，來歷少誤，勘核隨之矣，其何以得士耶？斯則雖遇李牧、虞詡，弗能展也。任將之道，其猶有未盡乎！
方今皇上當大德受命之初，正聖作物覩之會，薄海內外，罔不臣服。雖俺荅素雄漠北，亦歸心輸款，奉貢稱臣，四海無虞，休哉盛矣！然狼子野心，非我族類，窺覘虛實，無日無之。則除戎器、戒不虞，固今日之當務；而選將材、備任用，尤今日之所當豫圖者也。邇者聖謨加恤，廟議協心，分遣大臣巡行各邊，飭諸將，閱戎行，覸城堡，備
translation_en:
… pacify the Qiang. Both of these generals acted outside standard regulations; yet because their two rulers granted them that latitude, they were ultimately able to establish great achievements. Can those who appoint generals today give them free rein over money and grain without nitpicking? If they spend a single sum and the account registers are slightly off, the statutory rules are used to bind them—how then can they nurture their troops? Can we entrust them with recruiting soldiers without second-guessing? If they employ a single man and his background is slightly amiss, an investigation and audit immediately follow—how then can they win the services of capable men? Under such circumstances, even if one were to encounter a Li Mu 李牧 or a Yu Xu 虞詡, they would be unable to unfold their talents. Has the proper way of employing generals still not been fully realized?

At present, His Majesty is at the very beginning of receiving the Mandate through his great virtue, precisely at the juncture when the Sage arises and all creatures behold him; within and beyond the seas, there is none who does not submit as a subject. Even Altan Khan (Anda 俺荅), long dominant north of the desert, has turned his heart to us and pledged allegiance, presenting tribute and declaring himself a vassal. Within the Four Seas there is no cause for alarm—how splendid, how flourishing! Yet the wolf cub has a wild heart, and they are not of our kind; not a day goes by that they do not spy upon our strengths and weaknesses. Thus, readying military equipment and guarding against the unexpected are certainly urgent tasks for today, while selecting generalship material and preparing them for appointment are especially matters that must be planned for in advance today. Recently, His Majesty's sagely counsels have shown increased solicitude, and the court deliberations have been of one mind: Grand Ministers have been separately dispatched to tour the various frontiers, admonish the generals, inspect the ranks, survey the fortifications, and prepare …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
貯積申嚴之政視昔有加此即成王制治
保邦之良規周公克詰張皇之懿軌也復
允言官之請
令內而九卿百執事外而兩畿十三省卿士
牧伯各舉所知其求之固云廣矣然其所
選之者必得忠賢之將而舉之以為
國用下則秉忠以立身上則盡忠以報
國不以
朝廷之爵祿私吾身而以吾之一身為
===
朝廷效力於之未立不敢愛吾身而畏縮功
之既成不敢縱吾身而驕怠心乎為國而
吾身之死生以之則所謂智仁信勇嚴理
備果戒約者皆得以效于時而後其所以
選之者為不虛矣若夫營營于鑽刺者是
武弁中之細人也矜矜于文墨者是武弁
中之迂士也如是而欲置諸大用可乎其
所任之者必得忠賢之將而專委之閫外
內則不惑于浮言外則不制以遙斷不以
punctuated: 貯積，申嚴之政視昔有加。此即成王制治保邦之良規、周公克詰張皇之懿軌也。復允言官之請，令內而九卿百執事，外而兩畿十三省卿士牧伯，各舉所知，其求之固云廣矣。然其所選之者，必得忠賢之將，而舉之以為國用：下則秉忠以立身，上則盡忠以報國；不以朝廷之爵祿私吾身，而以吾之一身為朝廷效力；於之未立，不敢愛吾身而畏縮；功之既成，不敢縱吾身而驕怠；心乎為國，而吾身之死生以之。則所謂智、仁、信、勇、嚴、理、備、果、戒、約者，皆得以效于時，而後其所以選之者為不虛矣。若夫營營于鑽刺者，是武弁中之細人也；矜矜于文墨者，是武弁中之迂士也。如是而欲置諸大用，可乎？其所任之者，必得忠賢之將，而專委之閫外：內則不惑于浮言，外則不制以遙斷；不以
translation_en: …store provisions, with policies of renewed strictness surpassing those of the past. This is indeed the fine model of King Cheng for establishing order and securing the state, and the admirable course of the Duke of Zhou in thoroughly investigating the army and glorifying the six armies. Furthermore, approving the request of the speaking officials, an order has been issued that within the court the Nine Chief Ministers and the various functionaries, and in the provinces the high officials and regional governors of the Two Metropolitan Areas and the Thirteen Provinces, should each recommend those whom they know; the search for talent may certainly be called broad. Yet in selecting them, one must obtain loyal and worthy generals and recommend them for the use of the state: below, they hold fast to loyalty to establish themselves; above, they exhaust their loyalty to repay the state. They do not treat the ranks and emoluments of the court as private possessions for their own persons, but dedicate their own persons to exerting strength for the court. When merit [?] has not yet been established, they dare not cherish their own persons and shrink back in fear; when merit has already been achieved, they dare not indulge their own persons and become arrogant and lax. Their hearts are set on serving the state, and they stake the life and death of their own persons upon it. Then what are called wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, courage, strictness, orderliness, preparedness, resoluteness, vigilance, and frugality can all be put into effect in their time, and only then will the purpose for which they were selected not be in vain. As for those who busily scheme for advancement through intrigue, they are petty men among military officers; those who pride themselves on literary ink, they are pedantic scholars among military officers. Being like this, can one wish to place them in positions of great use? In employing them, one must obtain loyal and worthy generals and entrust them exclusively with commands beyond the threshold: within the court, do not be misled by baseless talk; outside, do not restrict them with remote decisions from afar; do not on account of…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
武弁之粗卒輕其任而以三軍之事爲將
帥作氣勿以拘攣執滯而阻其雄心勿以
禮節文移而責其細過重其責任而以邊
事之安危付之則所謂智仁信勇嚴理備
果戒約者皆得以盡其用而後其所以任
之者爲不輕矣若以一衣一食而檢之是
使之無以爲生也以一人一馬而稽之是
使之無以爲用也如是而欲得其死力可
乎雖然內有張仲而後吉甫得以成其功
===
內有魏相而後充國得以盡其策然非周
宣之賢漢宣之明有以主之于上則亦未
有能濟者也然則忠賢之將所以選之任
之而鼓舞之以成其用者惟吾
君吾相留意焉愚生行當繼江漢之詩作鼓鐃
之歌以
獻執事其肯轉
聞之否
punctuated: 武弁之粗卒輕其任，而以三軍之事爲將帥作氣；勿以拘攣執滯而阻其雄心，勿以禮節文移而責其細過。重其責任而以邊事之安危付之，則所謂智、仁、信、勇、嚴、理、備、果、戒、約者，皆得以盡其用，而後其所以任之者爲不輕矣。若以一衣一食而檢之，是使之無以爲生也；以一人一馬而稽之，是使之無以爲用也。如是而欲得其死力，可乎？雖然，內有張仲而後吉甫得以成其功，內有魏相而後充國得以盡其策，然非周宣之賢、漢宣之明有以主之于上，則亦未有能濟者也。然則忠賢之將，所以選之、任之而鼓舞之以成其用者，惟吾君、吾相留意焉。愚生行當繼《江漢》之詩，作鼓鐃之歌以獻，執事其肯轉聞之否？
translation_en: …the coarse abruptness of military officers, do not treat their commission lightly, but rouse the morale of the generals and commanders with the affairs of the Three Armies; do not thwart their ambitious spirit with narrow-minded constraints and rigid pedantry, nor fault them for minor transgressions in matters of etiquette and official correspondence. Give weight to their responsibilities and entrust them with the safety and peril of frontier affairs; then those qualities known as wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, courage, strictness, orderliness, preparedness, resoluteness, vigilance, and frugality will all be able to be put to their fullest use, and only then will the way in which they are employed not be taken lightly. If one scrutinizes them over every single garment and meal, this leaves them no means to make a living; if one audits them over every single man and horse, this leaves them no means to function. To act in such a manner and yet wish to obtain their service to the death—how could that be possible? Even so, it was only because Zhang Zhong 張仲 was at court within that Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 was able to achieve his merit abroad, and only because Wei Xiang 魏相 was at court within that Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 was able to carry out his plans to the fullest. Yet had it not been for the worthiness of King Xuan of Zhou 周宣王 and the discernment of Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝 presiding over them from above, neither would they have been able to succeed. This being so, as for how loyal and worthy generals are selected, entrusted with office, and inspired so as to bring their service to completion—may our Sovereign and our Grand Secretaries give their attention to this. This foolish student shall before long continue the ode "Jiang Han" 江漢 and compose martial songs for the drums and cymbals to present; would Your Excellencies be willing to transmit them to the throne?

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
今天子萬曆紀元之秋天下復當
鄉舉士于時巡按河南監察
御史褚〔鈇〕秉憲貞度終始乃
罔不肅既已竣事成錄〔邦〕不
佞濫從校藝之役敢附言末
簡以申告于多士夫上之所
===
需于士者才也士之所以厚
自負以需用于上者亦才也
才之難蓋自古然矣故百里
一士不異比肩而立乃梁豫
之士顧彬彬如此也何哉才
之產也未有不本于地而成
于時者干霄之木植必崇岡
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

今天子萬曆紀元之秋，天下復當鄉舉士。于時，巡按河南監察御史褚〔鈇〕秉憲貞度，終始乃罔不肅。既已竣事成錄，〔邦〕不佞，濫從校藝之役，敢附言末簡，以申告于多士。夫上之所需于士者，才也；士之所以厚自負，以需用于上者，亦才也。才之難，蓋自古然矣，故百里一士，不異比肩而立。乃梁豫之士，顧彬彬如此也，何哉？才之產也，未有不本于地而成于時者。干霄之木，植必崇岡；
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the first year of the Wanli reign of the reigning Son of Heaven, the empire once again held the Provincial Examinations to select scholars. At this time, the Regional Inspector of Henan and Investigating Censor Chu [Fu 褚鈇] upheld the laws and rectified the standards, ensuring that from beginning to end there was nothing that was not conducted with solemnity. Now that the affair has been completed and the record compiled, I, [Bang 邦], unworthy as I am, having undeservedly participated in the task of evaluating the literary compositions, venture to append my words at the end of the volume so as to address the many scholars.

Now, what the ruler requires of scholars is talent; and that by which scholars hold themselves in high regard while awaiting employment by the ruler is likewise talent. The scarcity of talent has indeed been so since antiquity; thus, finding one true scholar within a hundred li is no different from standing shoulder to shoulder. Yet the scholars of Liang and Yu [Henan] are, on the contrary, so flourishing in both refinement and substance as this—why is that? In the production of talent, there has never been a case where it was not rooted in the land and brought to completion by the times. Trees that brush the skies are surely planted on lofty ridges; …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
連城之璧毓必靈壤百卉春
華蜉蝣陰出夫物則亦有然
者矣九域分州而豫適當陰
陽風雨之所交會蓋稱天地
中焉是以河洛啓文明之瑞
嵩高標峻極之神詩書所述
自古爲烈矣歷代翼運興邦
===
陳謨佐治燁然光史冊爲世
望者以大都論不啻得什五
焉豈與夫遐陬僻區必間代
乃才一見者偶哉若是雖謂
梁豫爲才藪可也
國朝文治融朗聲敎四暨薄海
內外罔弗喁喁嚮風而豫介
punctuated: ，連城之璧毓必靈壤，百卉春華，蜉蝣陰出，夫物則亦有然者矣。九域分州，而豫適當陰陽風雨之所交會，蓋稱天地中焉。是以河、洛啓文明之瑞，嵩高標峻極之神，《詩》《書》所述，自古爲烈矣。歷代翼運興邦，陳謨佐治，燁然光史冊、爲世望者，以大都論，不啻得什五焉。豈與夫遐陬僻區，必間代乃才一見者偶哉？若是，雖謂梁、豫爲才藪可也。國朝文治融朗，聲敎四暨，薄海內外，罔弗喁喁嚮風，而豫介…
translation_en: … and jade discs worth a string of cities are necessarily nurtured in numinous soil; the hundred plants blossom in spring, while mayflies emerge in the shade—such is also true of natural things. When the Nine Regions were divided into provinces, Yu [Henan] lay precisely where yin and yang, wind and rain converge, and was thus called the center of Heaven and Earth. Therefore, the Yellow and Luo Rivers revealed the auspicious signs of civilization, and lofty Mount Song marked the sacred peak reaching to the heavens; as recounted in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) and the Classic of Documents (Shujing), its glory has been great since antiquity. Across the dynasties, those who assisted the Mandate to raise up the state, presented counsels to aid in governance, shone brilliantly in the pages of history, and stood as models for their ages—speaking in general terms, no less than half of them came from here. How could it be put on a par with distant corners and remote regions, where a talent appears only once in alternating generations? Since this is so, even to call Liang and Yu [Henan] a reservoir of talent is fitting. Under Our Dynasty, civil governance is radiant and clear, and its prestige and teachings extend in all four directions; within and beyond the four seas, there are none who do not eagerly look toward its transforming influence, and Yu lies situated…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
在
二都之中浸灌薰陶既深且速
是以豪雋挺生人文煥發若
鈞陽宣屛翰之烈嬔盛甫申
河内繹性命之精紹宗伊洛
祥符信陽含風咀雅則藝苑
之雄也安陽浚儀規言矩行
則人倫之範也炳燿鏗鍧震
眩耳目有更僕未易數者多
士沉酣
醲化加以淵源所漸觀感所興
又非一朝夕故其蔚然競爽
固其所也夫有司者爲
國掄才其始也蓋皆惴惴焉以
punctuated: 在二都之中，浸灌薰陶，既深且速。是以豪雋挺生，人文煥發。若鈞陽宣屛翰之烈，嬔盛甫、申；河内繹性命之精，紹宗伊、洛；祥符、信陽含風咀雅，則藝苑之雄也；安陽、浚儀規言矩行，則人倫之範也。炳燿鏗鍧，震眩耳目，有更僕未易數者。多士沉酣醲化，加以淵源所漸，觀感所興，又非一朝夕，故其蔚然競爽，固其所也。夫有司者爲國掄才，其始也，蓋皆惴惴焉以
translation_en: …is situated between the Two Capitals, so its immersion and nurturing in imperial influence have been both deep and swift. For this reason, outstanding talents have sprung forth and cultural refinement has shone brilliantly. For instance, Junyang [Ma Wensheng 馬文升] displayed the illustrious achievements of a bulwark of the state, rivaling the splendor of Fu [Zhongshan Fu] and Shen [the Marquis of Shen]; Henei [He Tang 何瑭 or Xue Xuan's followers] unraveled the essence of human nature and destiny, carrying on the lineage of the Yi and Luo rivers [the Cheng brothers]; Xiangfu [Li Mengyang 李夢陽] and Xinyang [He Jingming 何景明] savored the Airs and chewed upon the Odes, standing as champions of the literary realm; Anyang [Cui Xian 崔銑] and Junyi [Wang Tingxiang 王廷相] spoke by the compass and acted by the square, serving as models for human relationships. Resplendent and resonant, dazzling the eyes and ears, such figures are too numerous to count even if one were to change attendants in the telling. The many scholars here have been steeped in the dynasty's rich transformative influence, and furthermore, what they have gradually absorbed from these intellectual lineages and what has inspired them through observation and emulation is not the work of a single morning or evening; thus, that they flourish in vibrant competition is only natural. Now, when the authorities select talent for the State, at the outset they are all filled with trepidation, …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
求之不得爲懼既而縱觀多
士之所以自獻若啓武庫
之藏而璵璠溢璧遊鄧林之
區而楩楠彌野則又大喜過
望而復惴惴焉以有才而不
獲盡舉之爲憂夫果才之衆
也而不能盡舉之有司雖患
===
之無如何也
制也設若以才舉矣𧶘厥終逌
罔才焉則有司者不明之辠
將安逭之故願諸士之能自
成其信也蓋多才之域匪獨
有司者品藻之難郎士之自
立斬以才稱于鄉黨亦難昔
punctuated: 求之不得爲懼。既而縱觀多士之所以自獻，若啓武庫之藏而璵璠溢璧，遊鄧林之區而楩楠彌野，則又大喜過望；而復惴惴焉，以有才而不獲盡舉之爲憂。夫果才之衆也，而不能盡舉之，有司雖患之，無如何也，制也。設若以才舉矣，𧶘厥終逌罔才焉，則有司者不明之辠，將安逭之？故願諸士之能自成其信也。蓋多才之域，匪獨有司者品藻之難，郎士之自立，斬以才稱于鄉黨亦難。昔
translation_en: …fear that they might fail to find any. Yet when they subsequently surveyed what the many scholars presented of themselves—as if opening the stores of an armory to find precious jades overflowing the walls, or roaming the expanse of the Deng Forest to find fine hardwoods filling the wilderness—they were overjoyed beyond all expectation; and then once again they became anxious, worrying that where talent existed they would not be able to recommend it all. Now, if talent is indeed so abundant and yet cannot all be recommended, even though the authorities are troubled by this, there is nothing they can do about it: such is the quota system established by imperial regulation. Suppose, however, that men have been recommended for their talent, yet when one examines how they end up, they turn out to lack talent after all—then how shall the authorities escape the guilt of lacking discernment? Therefore, I wish for all you scholars to be able to fulfill and validate the trust placed in you through your own efforts. For in a region abundant in talent, not only is it difficult for the authorities to evaluate and grade men, even for a scholar to establish himself and aspire to be praised for talent in his own home community is difficult as well. In antiquity, …

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
周之東魯宋衛鄭號爲知禮
之國其卿士出入容止辭命
類恂雅有度一或舉足出口
毫髮有偬則不崇朝而傳詬
四國矣秦使適至終鮮戾
于儀而東國君臣至動色敬
異夫西鄙紹介縱能矜持中
===
禮亦豈若東卿士之從容哉
東卿士而若斯將中猶不免
有傳詬者在而奚至舉國敬
異之也此其故可知也布衣
韋帶之士有能自奮于畎畝
者苟行能脩潔即見稱于閭
井若夫衣冠故家之裔雖偉
punctuated: 周之東，魯、宋、衛、鄭號爲知禮之國，其卿士出入容止、辭命，類恂雅有度。一或舉足出口，毫髮有偬，則不崇朝而傳詬四國矣。秦使適至，終鮮戾于儀，而東國君臣至動色敬異。夫西鄙紹介，縱能矜持中禮，亦豈若東卿士之從容哉？東卿士而若斯，將中猶不免有傳詬者在，而奚至舉國敬異之也？此其故可知也。布衣韋帶之士，有能自奮于畎畝者，苟行能脩潔，即見稱于閭井；若夫衣冠故家之裔，雖偉
translation_en: …After the Zhou moved east, Lu, Song, Wei, and Zheng were renowned as states that understood ritual propriety. In their comings and goings, their demeanor and diplomatic speeches, their ministers and noblemen were generally sincere, refined, and measured. Yet if even once, in lifting a foot or uttering a word, there was the slightest haste or slip, before the morning was out derision would spread across the four states. When an envoy from Qin happened to arrive and throughout his visit rarely transgressed ritual decorum, the rulers and ministers of the eastern states were moved to visible awe and admiration. Now, even if an intermediary from the western marches could maintain his composure so as to hit the mark of ritual propriety, how could he match the effortless poise of the ministers and noblemen of the east? Had a minister or nobleman of the east behaved like that, there would still inevitably have been those within who spread derision—how would it ever have come to the entire state holding him in awe and admiration? The reason for this is easy to see. Among scholars in plain cloth and leather belts, if someone manages to rouse himself from the furrowed fields, so long as his conduct and abilities are cultivated and pure, he is immediately praised in his village community. As for the descendants of illustrious old families of official rank, even if they grandly…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
自表樹但其勳績稍不逮前
人則世必以爲不克紹厥家
聲爾矣多士之才于此中邦
也是東國卿士之于禮儀也
是故家子弟之于世德也人
之責備不以他邦域論矣而
可不矢所以自殖乎有其質
===
必思有以成其質有其言必
思有以踐其言懋德勵行績
學廣業必以古今先正所以
爲天下望者自待庶幾哉東
卿士之動容卒度而衣冠裔
之克世其家也有司者之獲
從事于多才之域不其爲大
punctuated: 自表樹，但其勳績稍不逮前人，則世必以爲不克紹厥家聲爾矣。多士之才于此中邦也，是東國卿士之于禮儀也，是故家子弟之于世德也，人之責備不以他邦域論矣，而可不矢所以自殖乎？有其質，必思有以成其質；有其言，必思有以踐其言。懋德勵行，績學廣業，必以古今先正所以爲天下望者自待，庶幾哉東卿士之動容卒度，而衣冠裔之克世其家也！有司者之獲從事于多才之域，不其爲大
translation_en: …distinguish themselves, yet if their meritorious achievements fall even slightly short of their predecessors, the world will surely consider them unable to carry on their family reputation. The talent of the many scholars here in this Central Region is like the minister-nobles of the Eastern States with respect to ritual and etiquette, and like the sons and younger brothers of established families with respect to hereditary virtue. People's expectations of perfection from them cannot be measured by the standards of other regions—so how can they not swear to cultivate and enrich themselves? Possessing the native substance, they must think of how to bring that substance to completion; possessing the words, they must think of how to put those words into practice. Striving for virtue and encouraging good conduct, accumulating learning and broadening their enterprise, they must hold themselves to the standard of how the former worthies of antiquity and the present became the hope of the Empire. Then, perhaps, they will be like the minister-nobles of the East whose every movement and deportment conformed wholly to the rules, and like the descendants of official families who are able to perpetuate their house across generations! For the authorities to be able to carry out their duties in a region of such abundant talent—is it not a great…

title: 萬曆元年河南鄉試錄
text:
幸乎否則無論隳窳不脩即
沾沾自喜而靳于宏到雖亦
隨時取聲譽乃所就畢畢將
不免傳詬四國而貽不克紹
之誚有司者之懼滋深矣嗚
呼多士尚敬勗之毋以才自
恃也
應天府六合縣儒學教諭吳
邦　謹序
punctuated:
幸乎！否則，無論隳窳不脩，即沾沾自喜而靳于宏到，雖亦隨時取聲譽，乃所就畢畢，將不免傳詬四國，而貽不克紹之誚，有司者之懼滋深矣。嗚呼！多士尚敬勗之，毋以才自恃也。
應天府六合縣儒學教諭吳邦謹序。
translation_en:
…great fortune! Otherwise, to say nothing of those who fall into sloth and fail to cultivate themselves, even if one is merely smugly self-satisfied and stops short of reaching great and far-reaching attainment—though one may still gain passing renown with the times, what is ultimately achieved will be paltry [? 畢畢, likely for 卑卑], and one will inevitably incur the reproach of the four quarters of the realm and leave behind the blame of having failed to carry on the ancestral legacy; then the dread of the officials in charge would only grow deeper. Alas! May the many scholars reverently exert themselves, and not presume upon their talents alone.

Respectfully prefaced by Wu Bang 吳邦, Instructor of the Confucian School of Liuhe County in Yingtian Prefecture.
